title: Assessing the estimands and estimates of hospitalization rates in health economics and clinical medicine
abstract: Even though data on hospital admissions are widely used in health research, hospitalization‐related estimands measured using these data are not always clearly conceptualized. Consequently, estimators of these quantities can have unclear rationales and undesirable properties. We evaluate three “rate” estimators for measuring hospitalization‐related estimands. Using the Gross-man human capital model, we motivate the importance of measuring healthy time. We show that an upper bound on healthytime can be calculated using lengths of hospital stay without assumptions about health status outside the hospital. We illustratethe empirical value of these bounds. Next, we find that an admission rate conventionally used in clinical research is a patient follow‐up time weighted average that lacks a clear basis for the weights. We propose an alternative estimator with more desirable properties and weaker assumptions. We assess its performance using a model of hospital admissions and death. Finally, we evaluate the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) use of risk‐standardized readmission rates to penalize hospitals by showing that risk‐standardized rates can be sensitive to patient case mix, potentially leading to hospital rankings that do not reflect hospital quality. We propose treating hospital specific intercepts in the CMS risk‐standardization model as a measure of quality.

title: Early interaction among public and private actors in public procurement: a boundary work perspective
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the boundary work strategies of buyers and suppliers during the early interaction phases of the public procurement process. It also examines how those strategies influence the transition from traditional arm’s-length interaction to relational interaction. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative embedded case study examines boundary work in the early phases of public procurement of catering and home nursing services. Findings The pre-tender phase requires balancing formal procurement rules and relational practices, which can hamper the boundary work that promotes relational interaction. The early post-tender phase complements the pre-tender phase by promoting relational interaction, considering that suitable boundary work strategies are applied. Practical implications This study provides insights into how boundary work strategies applied influence relational interaction in public procurement. Trust-building and a rethinking of established procurement practices are necessary to implement relational pre-tender interactions without compromising equality principles. Early post-tender interaction is critical in strengthening collaboration and addressing challenges inherent in the pre-tender phase. Social implications This study provides insights into the challenges of the early phases of interaction in public procurement, addressing the gap between policy goals and their implementation. Originality/value This study contributes to public–private interaction research by conceptualising dynamic interaction patterns and how they emerge in the early phases of the procurement process and to the understanding of relational interaction development by demonstrating the influence of multi-organisational boundaries on such interaction. The study highlights the role of early post-tender interaction in boundary-crossing.

title: Emerging Trends in Financial Reporting and Accountancy: Digital Transformation, Sustainability, and Regulatory Dynamics
abstract: Abstract The landscape of accountancy and financial reporting has undergone a monumental shift driven by rapid technological advancements, evolving regulatory frameworks, and increasing demand for corporate transparency. Traditional financial reporting models are shifting toward real-time data access, automated audit trails, and integrated non-financial disclosures. This research paper examines the convergence of automation, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Sustainable Financial Reporting (ESG disclosures) within modern accounting practices. It highlights key challenges faced by organizations during implementation and presents a prospective framework for accounting professionals to navigate digital disruption while maintaining reporting accuracy, transparency, and compliance.

title: Effect of financial risk on regional financial integration in Africa
abstract: The study examined the effects of financial risk on African regional financial integration covering 2008–2024. The study used panel regression analysis to assess the effect of loan default, delayed payments, losses from currency control, and expropriation of private investment on net capital inflow in South Africa and Nigeria. Loan default, payment delay, and expropriation of private investment all intensely reduce net capital inflow by -2.97%, -2.98%, and -2.02%, respectively, according to the research. Nevertheless, net capital inflow is positively affected, albeit somewhat, by losses from exchange control. The study established that there is a correlation between financial risk and the amount of investment flowing into Africa. More investment in Africa can only be encouraged if profit repatriation regulations are relaxed and loans are repaid on time.

title: EVALUATION AND MANAGEMENT OF SLEEP PROBLEMS IN CHILDREN WITH NEURODISABILITY: A LITERATURE REVIEW.
abstract: This literature review aimed to raise awareness of the current knowledge in the field of sleep disorders, which describes the complex relationship among child’s behavior, cognition and neurodevelopmental outcome. Sleep disorders associated with pediatric neurodisabilites and common neurological conditions causing sleep problems in children are discussed briefly in this article. Especial emphasis is given to an evaluation of sleep pattern recognition in children with neurodisabilites. We also summarized a broad range of management plans for child and family/caregivers. Some essential neurological conditions are highlighted as they provide useful insights into how disturbed sleep can impact on the cognitive and behavioral development of a child. Many neurological disorders exist along with sleep disorders such as epilepsy, autism, Cerebral palsy, etc., which carry profound effect on underlying child’s cognitive or behavioral pattern. The literature review is based on extensive literature search and author’s special interest in sleep disorders and pediatric neurodisabilites.

title: Damned if you do, damned if you don’t: the interpretive dilemma of strategic and compassionate leadership
abstract: Purpose This paper challenges the perceived antagonism between strategic leadership and compassionate leadership. It argues that the tension is not inevitable in organizational decision-making, but arises from essentialist assumptions that treat strategy and compassion as fixed leadership attributes. Design/methodology/approach This scholarly essay develops a conceptual argument grounded in social constructionist and attributional perspectives on leadership. Organizational episodes are used illustratively, rather than as empirical cases, to show how leadership discourse and observer interpretation can produce and stabilize the apparent conflict between strategic and compassionate leadership. Findings Two leadership myths are identified: that strategy requires emotional distance and that compassion undermines strategic resolve. These myths are sustained through attributional habits, institutional reinforcement, professional socialization, and psychological defense. When leadership is reframed as interpretive rather than essential, the perceived incompatibility diminishes. Integration is shown to be provisional, audience-dependent, and contingent upon interpretation. Practical implications People in leadership positions cannot ensure that their actions will be interpreted as both strategically necessary and compassionately enacted, although framing, communication, and attention to process can influence those judgments. More broadly, organizations, leadership development, and leadership scholarship can challenge the categories that present strategic resolve and compassion as opposing qualities. Social implications The paper reframes leadership as a site of ongoing public judgment, where authority and morality are continually contested rather than inherently possessed. Originality/value The paper applies a non-essentialist account of leadership to the strategy-compassion dilemma. It relocates the problem from how people in leadership positions balance supposedly competing qualities to how observers interpret the same action as strategic, compassionate, both, or neither. Reconciliation is therefore reframed as a provisional interpretive judgment rather than an integration of leadership attributes within the individual.
venue: Strategy and Leadership

title: Importance Of Science In National Development: Building The Foundation Of Viksit Bharat @2047
abstract: Abstract: Science has emerged as one of the most influential forces shaping economic growth, social transformation and national progress in the twenty-first century. The development of modern societies is increasingly dependent on the ability to create scientific knowledge, translate that knowledge into technological innovations and ensure that these innovations reach different sections of society. For a country such as India, which is simultaneously addressing issues of economic development, population growth, employment, education, healthcare, agriculture, energy security and environmental sustainability, science has a particularly important role to play. Scientific advancement can provide evidence-based and innovative solutions to complex national challenges while also strengthening India's competitiveness in the global knowledge economy. The vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 represents India's aspiration to become a developed nation by the centenary of independence. This vision encompasses not merely higher economic growth but also improvements in human development, education, healthcare, infrastructure, employment, social equity, technological capability, environmental sustainability and quality of life. Science and technology can serve as connecting forces among these different dimensions of development. Advances in agricultural science can improve productivity and climate resilience; medical science can support affordable healthcare; digital technologies can improve access to public services and education; space science can support communication, navigation and disaster management; renewable-energy research can strengthen energy security; and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, robotics and quantum technologies can create new opportunities for innovation and economic growth. The present paper examines the multidimensional importance of science in India's development with particular reference to Viksit Bharat @2047. It adopts a descriptive and analytical approach based on secondary information obtained from policy documents, government reports, scientific institutions, educational literature and international development reports. The paper discusses the contribution of science to economic development, agriculture, healthcare, education, industry, digital transformation, space technology, renewable energy and environmental sustainability. It further explores the role of scientific education in developing curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving ability and innovation among young people. The paper also identifies significant challenges, including unequal access to scientific resources, the digital divide, inadequate research infrastructure in some areas, limited industry-academia collaboration, shortage of specialised human resources, brain drain and the gap between scientific research and its practical application. The paper argues that the achievement of Viksit Bharat @2047 requires a transition from a technology-consuming society to a knowledge-generating and innovation-driven society. Strengthening scientific research, encouraging interdisciplinary collaboration, improving science education, supporting young researchers,

title: The Geometry of Bitcoin: Superlinear Feedback and the Finite-Time Singularity Problem
abstract: A working paper on intermittent superlinear feedback. A blow-up theorem: if the feedback exponent of dy/dx = k(1+y^m) fluctuates across the critical value m=1, a finite-time singularity follows almost surely, whatever the mean exponent — noise in the rate cannot do the same. With checkable membership conditions, a nested simulation, and candidate correspondences in tokamak edge instabilities and accelerating creep before slope failure. The construction originated in a study of Bitcoin's price geometry, which forms the first part.

title: EFFECT OF CIRCADIAN RHYTHM DISRUPTION ON FATIGUE AMONG PILOTS: NARRATIVE REVIEW
abstract: Background: The aviation environment exposes pilots to multiple circadian challenges including night operations, trans meridian travel, irregular scheduling, and fluctuating workload intensity. These factors contribute to acute and chronic fatigue, a recognized threat to operational safety and pilot health. Objective: This review synthesizes current scientific evidence on circadian rhythm biology, fatigue pathophysiology, demographic and operational risk determinants, and fatigue assessment tools, with a focus on applications to global aviation and emerging sectors such as Iraq. Methods: A narrative review approach was used to examine peer-reviewed studies published in aviation medicine, chronobiology, sleep research, and human factors. Databases searched included PubMed, Academic.edu, Aviat Space Environ Med, J Occup. Environ Med, SKY brary Aviation Safety, Elsevier Scopus, Web of Science, Web MD and Google Scholar. Study design included cross-sectional, cohort, review articles, thesis, survey, educational\ operational guidance, mixed method analysis and theoretical review in the last 20 years. Key finding: Findings demonstrate that circadian misalignment significantly impairs alertness, psychomotor function, decision-making, and sleep quality. Risk factors include age, chronotype, BMI, underlying medical conditions, night duties, long-haul operations, and environmental stressors. Validated tools such as the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) remain central to fatigue evaluation. Conclusion: For rapidly developing aviation sectors, including Iraq, implementing a layered, evidence-based fatigue management strategy is essential to improve safety, enhance pilot performance, and protect long-term pilot health, as fatigue is a hazard that can be anticipated, prevented, and managed.

title: A comparative study of human and AI-assisted feedback on Saudi EFL students' engagement and motivation in essay writing
abstract: This mixed-methods study examined how AI-assisted and human feedback influenced Saudi EFL students’ engagement and motivation in essay writing. Data were collected through surveys and semi-structured interviews. Quantitative findings showed similar overall engagement levels between students receiving AI feedback (M = 3.84) and those receiving human feedback (M = 3.83). Qualitative analysis revealed notable differences across engagement dimensions. AI feedback enhanced accessibility, provided immediate clarification, created opportunities for iterative revision, and offered emotional comfort during writing. In contrast, human feedback was valued for its personalization, contextual understanding, and social interaction. The findings also showed that students often adopted hybrid engagement practices by combining AI and human feedback to support their writing development. The study contributes empirical evidence to the growing literature on AI-assisted writing instruction and concludes by questioning the simplistic narratives about AI replacing humans. It provides a clear explanation of students’ engagement and motivation in AI-assisted writing instruction and offers practical advice for developing feedback in EFL writing classes.

title: Micro-foundations of sustainability: entrepreneurial identity and interaction patterns in plant-based food microenterprises
abstract: Purpose The paper aims to identify how entrepreneurs’ identities intersect with interaction patterns to facilitate sustainability-driven activities in microenterprises. In addition, it proposes a typology of sustainable entrepreneurs, ranging from Mission-Embedded Activists to Instrumentally Sustainable Entrepreneurs. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a qualitative study and presents the results of in-depth interviews conducted with entrepreneurs running 20 plant-based restaurant ventures, serving as a suitable context for examining sustainable entrepreneurship. Findings Sustainability-oriented activities in microenterprises emerge through the interplay between entrepreneurial identity, sustainability-driven identity and interaction patterns. This study develops and implements a four-part typology of sustainable entrepreneurs: Mission-Embedded Activists, Value-Oriented Practitioners, Health-Oriented Problem Solvers and Instrumentally Sustainable Entrepreneurs. Based on this typology, the study demonstrates how different identity configurations translate into distinct approaches toward actor selection, relational openness and the use of close cooperation and pure exchange interactions. The findings further show that interaction patterns are shaped not only by sustainability-driven values but also by resource availability, operational constraints and actors’ local proximity. Originality/value This paper advances understanding of sustainable entrepreneurs in microenterprises by demonstrating how entrepreneurial identity shapes interaction patterns and the enactment of sustainability-oriented activities. It contributes to the Industrial Marketing and Purchasing Group tradition by integrating entrepreneurial identity into the analysis of interaction, thereby extending micro-foundational perspectives in business network research. The study also shows that sustainability-oriented interaction patterns emerge through the interplay among identity, resource constraints and contextual conditions. Finally, it proposes a typology grounded in entrepreneurial identity and sustainability-driven identity, which is subsequently used to explain variation in interaction patterns across sustainable entrepreneurs.

title: From Dependence To Independence: Work, Economy, And The Changing Future Of Work In English Literature With Special Reference To Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre, Elizabeth Gaskell's North And South And Virginia Woolf's A Room Of One's Own
abstract: Literature is a mirror of society. It shows the economic conditions, social problems, and daily struggles of human life across different times. Work is one of the most important parts of human life. In the past, many people depended completely on land, rich masters, or family heads for their survival. Over time, the meaning of work has changed from total dependence to economic independence. English literature presents many stories of characters who fight against poverty and social rules to earn their own living and live with dignity. Work is not just a way to earn money; it also gives a person self-respect, identity, and personal freedom. This research paper examines how work, economy, and independence are presented in selected English literary texts: Charlotte Brontë’s Jane Eyre, Elizabeth Gaskell’s North and South, and Virginia Woolf’s A Room of One’s Own. These texts show how education, employment, and money help individuals to become free and confident. Finally, this paper connects these literary lessons with the modern world. Today, technology, artificial intelligence, online platforms, and work-from-home jobs are changing the future of work. The paper concludes that even in the modern digital age, human dignity and economic security are essential for true freedom.

title: Co-creating culturally safe primary care for whānau Māori with cancer: a qualitative case study of systems change in general practice
abstract: Introduction Māori experience later cancer diagnosis and poorer cancer outcomes than non-Māori. Although consultation-level cultural safety frameworks exist, less is known about embedding cultural safety across general practice to improve outcomes, guided by whānau (family) voices. Aim This study aimed to identify what culturally safe primary care looks like for whānau Māori with cancer, and to describe development of a whānau-led systems-change model within a single general practice. Methods A qualitative Kaupapa Māori (Māori approach) and Appreciative Inquiry study design was used. Māori patients with cancer, their whānau (family), and general practice staff participated in iterative phases of interviews and group hui. Reflexive thematic analysis and mahi ā rōpū (group work) informed theme development. A companion methods paper details methodology, data collection, and analysis. Results Whānau and staff described culturally safe care grounded in relationships, continuity, and environments that signal belonging. Through the research process, participants co-created a shared set of values and formed a whānau–staff working group that initiated practical changes in the clinic environment, access pathways, communication processes, and team culture. The project generated an actionable systems change model, demonstrating how cultural safety can potentially be embedded over time through sustained whānau involvement. Discussion This case study offers a pathway for general practices seeking to embed cultural safety at the service level. Practical considerations – leadership, commitment, whānau partnership, and willingness to address system constraints – are highlighted, and transferable pointers for other primary care services are outlined.
venue: Journal of Primary Health Care

title: Implementation Challenges of NEP 2020 in Indian Higher Education: A Critical Analysis of Academic Quality, Student Enrolment and Faculty Workload
abstract: Abstract: The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 is a landmark educational reform that aims to improve academic quality through multidisciplinary education, flexibility, research, innovation, digital learning, and skill-based education. Although the policy presents significant opportunities for transforming higher education, its implementation has created several practical challenges in higher education institutions, particularly aided colleges. This paper critically analyses the impact of NEP 2020 on student enrolment, faculty workload, curriculum overload, teacher surplus, skill-based education, and the rapid expansion of private colleges. The study concludes that academic quality can be achieved only through effective implementation, institutional accountability, and quality-oriented policy decisions rather than merely increasing the number of institutions.

title: A FRAMEWORK FOR INTERNET OF THINGS (IOT) ADOPTION AMONG STUDENTS AND STAFF OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS IN KEBBI STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) technologies are emerging that present great potential to transform higher education, including the concept of smart classrooms, intelligent laboratories, automated administration, campus resource management, environmental monitoring, and data-driven operations. Despite these advantages, the adoption of IoT in Nigerian higher education institutions (HEIs) particularly Kebbi State (HEIs) is still limited due to behavioural, technological, organizational and environmental factors. The study proposes the development of a UTAUT and TOE framework for modelling the adoption of IoT in Nigerian HEIs by combining the technology organization environment (TOE) and Unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT) framework. A quantitative survey design was used and data collected from 375 respondents, which included students, academicstaff and administrative staff of the HEIs in Kebbi State. The proposed relationships were assessed using statistical analysis. Results show that the factors of Performance Expectancy (β = 0.26), Effort Expectancy (β = 0.14), Facilitating Conditions (β = 0.18), Technological Factors (β = 0.17) and Organizational Factors (β = 0.23) have significant influence on IoT adoption while Social Influence (β = 0.05, p = 0.239) and Environmental Factors (β = 0.06, p = 0.153) are not. The model accounted for 64% (R2=0.64) of the variance in IoT adoption. The results indicate that perceived benefits, ease of use, enabling conditions, technological appropriateness, and organizational capability are key factors in the adoption of IoT in the Nigerian HEIs. The study offers an integrated and parsimonious model that integrates the acceptance of individual IoT devices with the conditions for institutional adoption and offers guidance to the university administrator, ICT manager, policymakers, and other stakeholders interested in supporting sustainable digital transformation using IoT technology.

title: The yin–yang of coopetition: reframing paradox in business-to-business marketing
abstract: Purpose This paper reframes coopetition, the simultaneous pursuit of cooperation and competition through the lens of Taoist yin–yang philosophy. This paper advances an ontologically explicit claim: that cooperation (yin) and competition (yang) stand in a relation of mutual entailment, such that one pole structurally generates the conditions for the other, rather than merely coexisting with it as in dualistic Western accounts. The purpose of this study is to show how this monistic ontology advances theory and practice in business-to-business (B2B) marketing. Design/methodology/approach A purposive systematic literature review structured by the theory–context–characteristics–method framework is conducted on foundational coopetition and paradox-theory works, supplemented by multi-industry evidence from technology alliances, pharmaceutical outsourcing and airline networks. Recent market data are used to illustrate measurable yin–yang dynamics in inter-firm relationships. Findings The study develops a monistic dynamic rebalancing model of coopetition, showing that firms achieve resilience and innovation not by eliminating tensions but by continuously shifting between cooperative and competitive logics that mutually entail one another. Industry evidence is consistent with the claim that coopetition is structurally embedded in B2B ecosystems, e.g. Apple and Samsung’s supply rivalry, pharmaceutical consortia feeding downstream exclusivity and airline alliances institutionalizing tension. Practical implications Managers should cultivate paradoxical cognition, design flexible structures and invest in dynamic capabilities that enable rebalancing across contexts. For B2B marketers, yin–yang thinking highlights how cooperation can strengthen differentiation and how rivalry can reinforce collaboration. Originality/value This paper develops an ontologically explicit monistic account of coopetition for B2B marketing, extending Eastern philosophical treatments of paradox from organization theory into the B2B marketing domain. The contribution is positioned as complementary-in-practice and distinct-in-ontology. Six falsifiable propositions are advanced; empirical validation is left to subsequent work.
venue: Journal of Business and Industrial Marketing

title: Making India a Knowledge Society in the Age of AI - Building India's Cognitive Infrastructure for Vikasit Bharat @2047
abstract: Abstract: This paper draws attention to the urgent need of building Cognitive Infrastructure along with the physical infrastructure for rapid development of the country. India is rapidly transitioning from developing economy to a developed economy unleashing many forces of rapid development and growth. The quest for Vikasit Bharat @2047 (India as a developed country) requires building the foundational cognitive-intellectual infrastructure and not just physical infrastructure. The development of the human capital with higher cognitive abilities capable to create, add and transact value through knowledge creation and utilisation. Continual innovation is critical for sustainable growth and development. Innovation is a direct outcome of the quality of the cognitive infrastructure. Nations compete on the strength of their cognitive infrastructure and not just on the availability of natural resources. Cognitive infrastructure is the most critical factor of production. To build a high-quality competitive cognitive infrastructure we need new ways of acquiring and utilising knowledge. Without cognitive abilities people cannot become knowledge workers to lead the cognitive shift happening all over the world in this age of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The race is now cognitive in nature and those nations with robust cognitive and physical infrastructure will be the leaders. India has to focus on developing the cognitive capital of the aspiring youth equipping the with cognitive abilities to respond to what is coming. The uncertainties caused by technological disruptions and geopolitical shifts are overwhelming. True security comes from building an ever-expanding and renewed cognitive infrastructure which is free from the laws of diminishing returns. This paper explores the need to take a fresh perspective of the emerging realities such as the shift from computing to cognitive, and recommends building futuristic cognitive infrastructure along with the physical infrastructure for realising the goal of Vikasit Bharat @2047. One core concern highlighted is the linguistic development as human development is fundamentally the cultivation of cognitive capacity—and language is one of the most powerful instruments for that cultivation.

title: ANATOMICAL UNDERSTANDING OF BHUJANGASANA IN INITIAL STAGES OF LUMBAR SPONDYLOSIS
abstract: Lumbar spondylosis, a degenerative condition affecting the intervertebral discs and facet joints of the lower spine, commonly presents with chronic low back pain, stiffness, and restricted mobility. In Ayurvedic and yogic rehabilitation, Bhujangāsana (Cobra Pose) is widely recommended as a therapeutic posture due to its spinal extension and strengthening effects. This asana gently mobilizes the lumbar vertebrae, stretches the anterior spinal structures, and strengthens the paraspinal and gluteal muscles, thereby improving lumbar stability. Regular practice helps to enhance inter vertebral space, reduce nerve root compression, and promote better postural alignment. Additionally, Bhujangasana increases blood circulation to the lumbosacral region, supports disc nutrition, and reduces muscular spasm. It's mindful breathing component further decreases pain perception by reducing stress-related muscle tension. Overall, Bhujangasana serves as an effective, non-invasive adjunct in the conservative management of lumbar spondylosis, contributing to pain reduction, improved flexibility, and enhanced functional outcomes. This article focuses on the anatomy and pathophysiology of lumbar spondylosis, its symptomatolgy and role of bhujangasana in it's management.

title: Quantifying Non-Profit Impact in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This methods preprint develops Net Attributable Value (NAV) for non-profit support to micro and small enterprises, combining explicit counterfactuals, contribution margins, attribution, displacement, persistence, survival and costs. It separates private contribution value from a displacement-adjusted producer-and-provider account. A stylised Indian printing-shop appraisal and a Monte Carlo comparison of revenue estimators illustrate the framework. All numerical exercises use simulated data and illustrative assumptions; the paper does not establish realised enterprise impact or a causal benefit of AI. Portfolio precision and detection thresholds are conditional on the specified data-generating process. The proposed measurement protocol and evidence grades require field validation. The deposit includes the corrected manuscript in PDF and editable DOCX, analysis.py, results.json, README.md and requirements.txt. The supplied code is a newly documented implementation of the stated model; the initial manuscript’s original script was unavailable. The revised manuscript reports the recomputed outputs and discloses AI assistance and the author’s organisational interest. This is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

title: Financial Inclusion by Design: A Policy Analysis of MUDRA Yojana's Formulation, Implementation, and Outcomes
abstract: Abstract India's Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises sector drives nearly a third of the country's Gross Value Added, yet as recently as 2015 almost 90% of these businesses had no access to formal credit. The Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), launched that year to fund this "unfunded" segment through collateral-free loans, has since grown into one of the world's largest micro-credit interventions — sanctioning over 52 crore loans worth more than ₹32–35 lakh crore in a decade. This study traces PMMY's policy design, its four-tier loan structure (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun, and the recently added Tarun Plus), and its performance from 2015-16 to 2024-25, drawing entirely on secondary data from official annual reports and peer-reviewed literature. The analysis finds a clear shift from micro-lending toward larger Kishore and Tarun loans, alongside strong inclusion of women (68–71% of accounts) and SC/ST/OBC borrowers (~50% of accounts). However, it also uncovers a persistent gap: these groups hold a disproportionate share of accounts relative to the credit value they actually receive, suggesting concentration in entry-level loans rather than genuine graduation to higher tiers.

title: SOCIAL MEDIA OVERUSE AS A POTENTIAL NIDANA FOR VATA PRAKOPA: AN INTEGRATIVE AYURVEDIC REVIEW
abstract: Ayurveda describes health as a dynamic equilibrium among the three doshas—Vata, Pitta, and Kapha—which govern physiological and psychological functions. Vata, composed primarily of Akash (space) and Vayu (air), regulates body like breathing, circulation, sensory perception, neuro- muscular activity, neural regulation, excretion and mental functions(like-enthusiasm, creativity, alertness, quick thinking).All these actions are essential for healthy body functioning. When Vata becomes aggravated (Vata vriddhi or Vata prakopa), clinical features such as restlessness, insomnia, anxiety, irregular appetite, dryness, fatigue, and impaired concentration commonly emerge. Contemporary lifestyles are increasingly dominated by social media platforms that encourage continuous engagement, rapid information switching, and prolonged screen exposure. Modern research associates excessive digital media use with psychological stress, sleep disruption, attention fragmentation, irritability, and anxiety—symptoms that closely relate to Ayurvedic descriptions of Vata imbalance. This integrative review examines parallels between Ayurvedic Vata pathophysiology and modern psychobehavioral literature on social media use. By mapping shared symptoms, changing lifestyle and potential preventive strategies, the article proposes a cross-disciplinary framework for understanding digital overuse as a contributing factor to Vata-type lifestyle disorders.

title: The Forbidden "Why" Question - From a Single Particle Universe to Space and Time
abstract: The Forbidden “Why?” Question — From a Single-Particle Universe to Space and Time Modern physics is extraordinarily successful at describing what happens once space, time, fields, particles, and mathematical structures are already available. But there is a more fundamental question that is rarely pursued to its logical beginning: Why is there a structure in which physical events can exist at all? This paper explores that question by considering an intentionally extreme starting point: a universe containing only a single fermionic degree of freedom. No second particle is assumed. No external detector is introduced. No Euclidean space is presupposed, and physical time is not taken as a primitive parameter. The starting point is the internal complex structure of a Dirac spinor and, in particular, the reciprocal relation between its two Weyl sectors. From the elementary relation Z+1/Z the paper investigates how reciprocal oscillation, differentiation, winding, indexing, and relational dynamics can generate distinctions that initially have no need to be interpreted as ordinary spatial or temporal structures. The central idea is that relation may precede geometry. A distinction between internally evolving sectors can generate a relational differential structure; topologically distinct winding sectors can subsequently become mutually related; and stable relations can then acquire the representation of space and time. In this view, spacetime is not introduced as the stage upon which the particle exists. It is investigated as a possible representation of stable relations generated by the underlying system. The construction connects naturally to the established CEGS–TSO framework, where compatible relational oscillations provide a route toward stable Euclidean spatial and temporal representations. The purpose here, however, is not to rederive all of TSO or quantum mechanics, but to investigate the deeper selfreferential starting point from which such structures might arise. The paper deliberately ends with open questions. In particular, it does not yet establish whether conservation of total energy follows from the winding structure itself, nor does it explain why the conversion between temporal and spatial representations introduces the physical constant c. These unresolved questions are not hidden limitations but part of the investigation: if the objective is to ask why, then unexplained constants and conservation laws cannot simply be declared fundamental and the inquiry stopped there. The result is therefore not presented as a final theory of the universe. It is a search for the beginning of physical description: an attempt to follow the chain backward from space and time toward the minimal relational structure from which they might emerge. The paper asks a simple question with unusually broad consequences: What is the minimum structure required before space and time can exist as meaningful concepts? This question points toward a deeper possibility: the underlying self-referential base of reality from which everything else may emerge. title: More, shorter, newer? How monetization reshapes creator strategy on YouTube Shorts
abstract: Purpose This study examines the causal impact of YouTube Shorts' ad-revenue sharing policy on creator production strategies in the short-form video creator economy. Design/methodology/approach Using 36,507 videos from 342 top global channels, we employ a regression discontinuity in time design. Computer vision techniques measure four attributes of each creator's production strategy: output volume, video length, editing pace, and content novelty. Findings The policy drove an immediate reduction in video length without expanding output volume, consistent with substitution toward cheaper per-unit configurations rather than output scaling. Entertainment creators shortened their videos most sharply, while informative creators slowed their editing pace to preserve comprehension. Long-type creators pursued per-unit cost reduction, while short-type creators invested in content novelty. Research limitations/implications The sample covers top-tier global channels, so emerging creators may respond differently. The findings show that the quantity-expansion result from low-marginal-cost user-generated content settings does not extend to high-marginal-cost production, where incentives reallocate effort within existing output rather than expand it. Practical implications A uniform monetization policy does not produce uniform outcomes. Incentive design should anticipate that creators adjust different production attributes depending on their content goals and capabilities. Originality/value This study provides causal evidence that performance-contingent monetization reshapes production strategy in a high-cost video production context and that one platform-wide policy generates different responses across creator types.

title: A HYBRID SIMULATION-OPTIMIZATION FRAMEWORK FOR PANDEMIC AND CRISIS RESPONSE: A RECONFIGURABLE SYSTEMS APPROACH
abstract: ABSTRACT: A Simulation-Optimization (SimOpt) framework reconfigures healthcare resources during pandemic crises via an analogy with Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems (RMS). The study formally establishes equivalence between Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems RMS reconfigurability and healthcare adaptability, then develops a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming MILP model optimized through Discrete Event Simulation. The methodology includes: (1) a conceptual mapping of six RMS characteristics to healthcare, (2) a validated DES model of an emergency department under crisis, and (3) a MILP model with 267 variables and 431 constraints, coupled via queueing-theory bounds. The framework achieves a 35.0% reduction in overall patient waiting times and a 44.3% improvement for critical patients, moving only 11 resource units across 6 transfers. All six RMS characteristics map directly onto quantifiable healthcare attributes, confirming operational validity. This is among the first studies to formally apply the RMS framework to healthcare operations using a validated SimOpt architecture. The work integrates industrial engineering, operations research, and healthcare management science, offering a practical tool for hospital crisis resource planning.

title: VISHADA: AN AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVE ON PSYCHOLOGICAL INHIBITION
abstract: Vishada is an Ayurvedic concept describing a state of mental disturbance in which emotional strength, confidence, initiative, and engagement with daily life becomes diminished. It extends beyond temporary sadness and involves changes in mental, behavioural and physical functioning. The present discussion explores the classical understanding of Vishada with emphasis on its etiopathogenesis and therapeutic perspective. Psychological experiences such as Ishta Viyoga and prolonged stress may disturb the equilibrium of Satwa and Tamas, with subsequent involvement of Manas, Vatadi doshas and Manovaha Srotas. Its manifestations, including Kaya-Vak-Manas Sada, Apravritti, Karyeshu Asiddhi Bhaya and impairment of Dhi, Dhriti, and Smriti demonstrate the wide-ranging influence of Vishada on activity, motivation, cognition, communication and social interaction. The Ayurvedic approach further emphasizes restoration of mental well-being through different lines of treatment. Understanding Vishada through this holistic framework highlights the close relationship between emotional experience and overall functioning and provides a foundation for its deeper exploration in contemporary mental-health research.

title: Late Pleistocene–Early Holocene Population Aggregation and Cultural Interaction on the Tibetan Plateau: A Testable Hypothesis for Human Mobility, Ritual Formation, and Post-Glacial Dispersal
abstract: The Tibetan Plateau is increasingly recognised as an important region in the long-term history of human adaptation, mobility, and population interaction in Asia. Archaeological evidence demonstrates that archaic hominins occupied parts of the plateau by at least 160,000 years ago and that modern humans were present in the interior from approximately 40,000–30,000 years ago, while ancient-DNA research has revealed substantial population structure and interaction on the plateau during the later Holocene. A major chronological gap remains, however, between the earliest evidence for human presence and the currently available ancient genomic record. This paper proposes a testable hypothesis concerning the possible role of the western Tibetan Plateau during the Late Pleistocene–Early Holocene transition. Rather than treating the plateau solely as an isolated ecological refuge, the paper considers whether parts of western Tibet may have functioned as a temporary, possibly seasonal, population aggregation and interaction zone during periods of climatic and hydrological instability. Under this model, environmental change redistributed the spatial distribution of key resources; populations responded by adjusting their mobility, repeatedly converging at newly favourable localities, and interacting before dispersing during the later Holocene. The model generates opportunities for demographic mixing, technological exchange, and the development or transformation of ritual practices, without requiring permanent high-density settlement or any single direction of transmission. The hypothesis does not claim that civilisation originated on the Tibetan Plateau. Three competing models are considered: transmission from West Asia towards the Tibetan Plateau; transmission from the Tibetan Plateau towards West Asia; and a third model involving broader interaction networks and/or independent cultural convergence. Archaeological chronology, palaeoenvironmental records, site occupation patterns, lithic technology, raw-material provenance, ancient DNA, and ritual evidence are assessed against a four-level classification (direct, compatible, suggestive, untested) to identify the evidence capable of distinguishing between these models. The paper presents an interdisciplinary research framework rather than a claim of historical proof. Its central contribution is to formulate a specific, falsifiable hypothesis — the seasonal aggregation-zone hypothesis — and to identify the archaeological and genetic evidence that would be required to support, modify, or reject it.

title: Optimization of Capital Structure for Student Housing through the Public–Private Partnership Model in Higher Educational Institutions
abstract: Abstract The public–private partnership (PPP) model can serve as a sustainable mechanism to bridge the funding deficit in higher educational institutions (HEIs). Profitability remains a primary objective that compels private partners to bear the risks inherent in this model. This study formulates an optimal PPP capital structure for student housing in Indian HEIs using the ant colony optimization (ACO) algorithm. A multiobjective model balancing private profitability, student affordability, and public funding was validated through a case study at Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras. The optimal solution, achieved at a 60% viability gap funding (VGF) level, a 5.55% loan rate, and a rent of USD 852, yielded an equity internal rate of return (EIRR) of 11.03%. The Pareto-front analysis further identified alternative optimal capital structures. Of the 41 feasible solutions, 23 were identified as Pareto-optimal, providing stakeholders with the flexibility to adopt the most suitable capital structure for each project. The nondominated solution set included alternatives with 80% and 60% viability gap funding at a 5.55% loan rate. The findings suggest that PPP-based student housing is financially viable and policy-ready. Student housing in India is a promising emerging real estate sector characterized by low risk, rising enrollment, and stable income streams.
venue: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Exploration of the Perspectives of Students, Teachers and Experts on Online Education under the National Education Policy 2020
abstract: Since the recent pandemic in India, the New Education Policy (NEP) and online education have truly emerged, advancing steadily each day. If we examine the current format of education, we can say that online education aligns meaningfully and compatibly with the present New Education Policy. The main objective of this research paper is to assess the reliability, authenticity, and significance of online education in conjunction with the New Education Policy, using various past research studies, references, conclusions, and experiences. This research paper will discuss a brief introduction to online education and the New Education Policy, along with tools, resources, challenges, progress, conclusions, etc. The obstacles in the path of online education and the New Education Policy reveal a significant difference between today's rural and urban environments, which will be highlighted as a limitation in this research paper. Observing past studies, we can conclude that online education and the New Education Policy will complement and enhance each other in the future. However, we cannot ignore the gaps that online education presents. Therefore, it can be said that online education has shown some significant positive outcomes, as well as some negative impacts.

title: Public Policy and Economic Reforms in India: An Assessment of Their Impact on Economic Growth and Development
abstract: Abstract Public policy and economic reforms have played a significant role in shaping India’s economic transformation, particularly since the introduction of the New Economic Policy in 1991. The reform process has progressively focused on liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation, fiscal restructuring, financial inclusion, digitalisation, investment promotion and strengthening the business environment. This study examines the role of public policy and economic reforms in promoting economic growth and development in India. The study is based on secondary data collected from official sources, including government publications, the Reserve Bank of India, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Ministry of Finance, NITI Aayog and international databases. Selected indicators such as GDP growth, per-capita income, foreign direct investment, tax revenue, financial inclusion and employment are analysed to assess the outcomes of policy reforms. The study indicates that economic reforms have contributed to greater market efficiency, investment, financial inclusion and economic integration. However, challenges relating to employment generation, income inequality, regional disparities and inclusive development continue to require policy attention. The study concludes that future economic reforms should focus not only on accelerating economic growth but also on ensuring inclusive, sustainable and broad-based development.

title: Building trust, bridging traditions: a story of collaborative instructional planning in a high school-university partnership
abstract: Purpose This article documents the collaboration between a high school social studies teacher and a university professor – working within an existing school-university partnership – in the design and implementation of a geography-based Holocaust lesson to support authentic learning opportunities for preservice teachers. This article responds to calls for educators in school-university partnerships to tell stories of the creation, evolution, challenges and possibilities of boundary-spanning partnership work. Design/methodology/approach The article utilizes storytelling as a means of documenting the importance of relationships in partnership work. Because storytelling is not dependent on traditional methods and frameworks, the authors outline the background, challenges and successes around their planning, coordination and implementation of an original lesson plan developed to model best practices on teaching difficult histories in a safe environment. Findings As a storytelling account, this work does not present empirical or generalizable findings. The story is offered as an example to foster reflection and conversation within other school-university partnerships. Originality/value Our narrative, which captures how relationships are central to partnerships, provides an illustrative example of how partnerships can support efforts to address gaps in education research and in modeling for preservice teachers for how to teach difficult histories in high school social studies classes. The authors reflect on how trust, shared expertise, reciprocal learning and collaboration can support meaningful, relevant and boundary-spanning experiences within partnerships between high schools and universities and colleges.

title: Explainable Hybrid AI for Detecting Ledger Manipulation in SME Accounting Systems: A Cyber-Forensic Framework Using Deep Autoencoders, XGBoost and SHAP
abstract: This working paper develops and evaluates an explainable hybrid artificial-intelligence framework for detecting anomalous general-ledger transactions in small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) accounting systems. A synthetic SME general ledger comprising 50,000 transactions across 400 accounts and 80 users was generated over the period 2022–2024, with approximately 2% controlled behavioural anomalies representing amount spikes, unusual posting hours, rare debit-credit account relationships and suspiciously round amounts.The framework combines Isolation Forest, a Deep Autoencoder, supervised XGBoost refinement and SHAP-based explainability. Ground-truth anomaly variables, anomaly categories, transaction descriptions, transaction identifiers and transaction-type labels were excluded from predictive model inputs. The models therefore operated on behavioural characteristics rather than descriptive anomaly indicators. Experimental evaluation used a chronological 70/15/15 training-validation-test design.On the held-out test set, the Hybrid Autoencoder–XGBoost model achieved precision of 0.646, recall of 0.329, F1 of 0.436 and PR-AUC of 0.359, with a final alert rate of 1.09%. Compared with the standalone Autoencoder, hybrid refinement reduced false-positive alerts from 118 to 29 while retaining 53 of 61 Autoencoder-detected anomalies.SHAP analysis identified credit-account frequency, debit-credit pair rarity, debit-account frequency and Autoencoder reconstruction error among the strongest contributors to model decisions. The study positions explainable hybrid AI as an auditor decision-support mechanism rather than as an autonomous determination of fraud.Supporting materials include synthetic data, experimental results, transaction-level test predictions, feature documentation, run metadata and explainability outputs. No real organisational records, confidential financial information or personal data were used.

title: India's Environmental Policies for Viksit Bharat @2047
abstract: Abstract India's developmental trajectory inevitably encounters the dual challenge of balancing poverty alleviation for one of the world's largest populations while avoiding the environmental consequences that have beset many industrialised nations. This paper explores how India's environmental policy architecture — from early conservation statutes to the recent suite of climate missions, the Panchamrit commitments, and the Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) movement — has evolved into an instrument of sustainable development rather than a constraint upon growth. The paper situates this policy architecture in India's long-term development blueprint, Viksit Bharat @2047, which envisions India as a fully developed nation by the hundredth anniversary of its independence. The paper argues that environmental sustainability is not a peripheral concern within Viksit Bharat 2047 but one of its structural pillars, since climate risk, resource security, and green industrial competitiveness will substantially determine whether India's growth is durable. The paper also identifies the principal obstacles — continued coal dependence, uneven state-level enforcement, financing gaps, and the need for a just transition for workers in carbon-intensive sectors — and closes with policy recommendations for aligning India's environmental governance more tightly with its 2047 ambitions.

title: The Red Thaw: Soviet climate science and the politics of global warming, 1950s–1991
abstract: Abstract This article examines how climate science developed in the Soviet Union from the 1950s to the early 1990s as a field shaped both by international scientific exchange and by the political priorities of the Soviet state. Focusing on the climatologist Mikhail Budyko and his research group at the State Hydrological Institute in Leningrad, it shows how Soviet scientists participated actively in emerging international discussions of anthropogenic climate change while working within institutions shaped by the priorities of socialist planning. Soviet climatologists were among the early contributors to the scientific analysis of global warming, yet they often interpreted its implications differently from their Western counterparts. In the USSR, warming was understood less as an environmental crisis than as a process compatible with long-term planning, technological intervention and, in some regions, potential economic benefit. Drawing on archival materials and interviews, the article traces how climate knowledge circulated between domestic and international scientific arenas while remaining shaped by the political culture of the late Soviet state. The Soviet case challenges narratives that explain political inaction on climate primarily through ignorance or denial, showing instead how the political significance of climate knowledge depended on the institutional frameworks through which it was interpreted and mobilized.
venue: The British Journal for the History of Science

title: Role of Sahakar Sarathi in Strengthening Digitalization of Rural Cooperative Banks
abstract: Even though rural cooperative banks are the institutional foot soldiers of the agricultural credit system in India, they have lagged behind the commercial banks in the use of technology and hence subjected to competitive erosion, operational inefficiencies and increasing cyber risk. To provide common core banking solutions, digital payment options, cybersecurity and IT governance support, and capacity building to the sector, in July of 2025, the Government of India through NABARD, the National Cooperative Development Corporation and the participating rural cooperative banks created the shared service entity known as Sahakar Sarathi Private Limited. This paper explores the potential of this institutional innovation to enhance the digitalization of rural cooperative banks and at what level. The study is a descriptive-cum-analytical type of study, which relies entirely on secondary data collected from the Reserve Bank of India, NABARD, the Ministry of Cooperation, National Payments Corporation of India and World Bank during the study period (2018-19 to 2025-26) and analyzed through percentage, growth-rate, trend and comparative techniques. The digital deficit in the sector is not attitudinal but structural, with the Unified Payments Interface alone handling 24162 crore transactions in 2025-26, which are very large in absolute numbers. The shared-cost architecture of Sahakar Sarathi directly targets this scale problem and operational feasibility is validated by the early deployment of payment and e-KYC services using Aadhaar. This is due to the limited availability of outcome information and the voluntary nature of participation, however, the paper concludes that the initiative's developmental promise is not guaranteed.

title: Transfer of Cognitive Authority: A Measurement Framework for the Closure of Artificial Intelligence Production
abstract: This manuscript proposes a measurement framework for studying the transfer of cognitive authority from human operators to increasingly autonomous artificial intelligence systems. The framework distinguishes capability from cognitive authority and models the transfer of cognitive functions through four operational components: problem selection (P), solution generation (S), evaluation (E), and recursive improvement (R). It introduces measures of human intervention, recursive contribution, evaluator independence, substitution recovery, generalization, and validated capability production. The central research question is whether increasingly autonomous AI systems can assume progressively more of the cognitive functions required not merely to perform tasks, but to produce, evaluate, and improve their own future capabilities. The manuscript develops falsifiable experimental designs, controlled ablation and substitution procedures, difficulty controls, evaluator-independence requirements, synthetic analyses, power considerations, and reproducibility procedures. Published empirical work concerning AI-assisted machine-learning research and autonomous AI research systems is discussed separately from the manuscript's synthetic analyses and proposed measurements. This work was developed with substantial assistance from generative artificial intelligence, including ChatGPT. AI assistance was used during conceptual exploration, literature-oriented research, mathematical formulation, experimental-design development, computational analysis, drafting, editing, and adversarial critique. The author retains responsibility for the final content, interpretation, limitations, citations, and conclusions.

title: Remittances under siege: how democracy and militarization shape economic growth in the world's top recipient nations
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the differential impact of remittances, democracy index, their interaction and gross militarization index (GMI) on economic growth across top remittance-receiving lower middle-income countries (LMICs). By dividing nations into two groups based on democracy levels, the research investigates whether institutional context – particularly democratic quality – moderates the remittance–growth relationship. Design/methodology/approach This quantitative study analyses panel data (2006–2023) from top remittance-receiving lower middle-income nations, split into high and low democracy groups. Estimation employs POLS, Fixed Effects and Random Effects models, with Hausman test guiding selection. The model incorporates remittances, democracy, GMI and their interaction. Robustness is addressed through 2SLS for endogeneity, slope homogeneity tests (Pesaran–Yamagata) and Kao–Pedroni cointegration tests, ensuring valid, reliable empirical findings across both institutional contexts. Findings Key findings reveal a democracy-based divergence: remittances and democracy negatively correlate with growth in high-democracy nations but positively in low-democracy countries. The interaction term is positive in democratic settings – suggesting synergy – yet negative in weaker democracies, indicating democratization without institutional capacity disrupts remittance effectiveness. GMI shows no significant growth impact. Long-run relationships are confirmed through cointegration. Endogeneity tests (Durbin and Wu-Hausman p > 0.05) confirm no endogeneity, validating panel regression results. These findings underscore the fact that institutional context fundamentally determines whether remittances contribute to productive investment or are absorbed into consumption. Research limitations/implications This research contributes to institutional economics by demonstrating that democracy's moderating role in the remittance–growth nexus is contingent on institutional quality. It challenges the assumption that democracy universally enhances remittance effectiveness, revealing instead that institutional capacity determines outcomes. The introduction of GMI as a novel variable adds to militarization literature, though its insignificance warrants further investigation across diverse contexts. Originality/value This research contributes original empirical evidence by examining the remittance–growth relationship through an institutional lens, comparing high versus low democracy nations. It introduces GMI as a novel variable in this context, addressing a critical gap in militarization literature. The study's comparative panel approach across democracy regimes, combined with rigorous robustness checks, offers fresh insights into how political context determines remittance effectiveness, informing both theory and policy.
venue: Journal of Economic Studies

title: An integrated framework for developing a national industrial technology roadmap: Thailand perspectives
abstract: Purpose This study aims to propose an integrated approach to roadmap development that enhances alignment and practical impact by combining data-driven analysis with stakeholder engagement. Design/methodology/approach The methodology incorporates drivers and trends analysis, social network analysis and technology readiness assessments into the roadmapping process. This approach is demonstrated through a roadmap development case of the automotive industry in Thailand. Findings This study presents the approach for establishing a national industrial technology roadmap that aligns the national goals with technology capabilities indicated through the assessment of technology readiness levels (TRLs) and uses the social network analysis to promote technological collaborations among stakeholders. Originality/value This study presents the integrated framework to formulate a national industrial technology roadmap as an integral component of broader national strategic planning aimed at enhancing technological capabilities and future preparedness. It presents a systematic approach to developing such a roadmap by aligning national objectives with TRLs. Social network analysis is also used to strengthen technological collaboration among key stakeholders.

title: I regulate my emotions; therefore, I am creative? Daily emotion regulation and workplace creativity
abstract: Purpose Evidence on the daily within-person relationship between emotion regulation strategies and creativity remains limited, particularly in non-service contexts. This study addresses this gap by examining the indirect relationship between day-level deep and surface acting and creativity via positive affect, and the moderating role of emotion regulation ability. Design/methodology/approach One-week diary study of 103 employees, analyzed using multilevel structural equation modeling. Findings Day-level deep acting was indirectly related to day-level creativity through positive affect, whereas surface acting showed the opposite pattern. Emotion regulation ability amplified the positive affective outcomes of day-level deep acting but did not buffer the negative effects of surface acting. Originality/value By examining how day-level deep and surface acting indirectly relate to creativity via positive affect in a non-service context, this study addresses a gap in research on day-level emotion regulation and creativity. Integrating broaden-and-build theory with emotion regulation research, it highlights emotion regulation ability as a personal resource amplifying the positive affective outcomes of deep acting.
venue: Journal of Managerial Psychology

title: Transforming management education in the Global South: empirical evidence on robotics-enabled embodied learning in economic universities
abstract: Abstract This article examines the role of robotics-enabled embodied learning in transforming management education within the Global South. As higher education institutions in developing and transition economies face increasing pressure to modernize curricula and cultivate digitally fluent, adaptive graduates, conventional pedagogical approaches often prove insufficient. Drawing on embodied cognition theory—which emphasizes the integration of mind, body, and environment in learning—this study positions robotics as a pedagogical medium capable of operationalizing experiential and practice-oriented management training. The study adopts a mixed-method research design with a dominant quantitative component, combining a cross-country survey of faculty and students in economic universities across four Global South countries with complementary conceptual and contextual analysis. Empirical findings indicate that the integration of robotics and embodied learning practices is positively associated with higher levels of student engagement, critical thinking, and perceived learning effectiveness. Regression analysis further demonstrates that institutional support, faculty training, and access to technological infrastructure are the strongest predictors of successful implementation. Beyond empirical validation, the article critically examines structural and policy-related barriers—such as uneven digital readiness and institutional capacity constraints—that mediate the adoption of robotics-based pedagogy in the Global South. By situating technological innovation within broader developmental and geopolitical contexts, the study advances a context-sensitive framework for management education reform. It contributes to the literature by linking embodied cognition and educational robotics to measurable learning outcomes, while offering actionable insights for universities and policymakers seeking to foster inclusive, future-ready management education systems.
venue: Asian Review of Political Economy

title: Evaluating the Burden of Non-Communicable Diseases in a Tertiary Hospital Setting: A Bangladesh Perspective.
abstract: In recent times, non-communicable diseases (NCDs) have emerged as a significant global public health challenge. Particularly impact in middle- and low-income countries, NCDs is responsible for 74.0% of global deaths, with South Asia, including Bangladesh, experiencing a mortality rate of 77.0%. Amidst an epidemiological transition, Bangladesh is witnessing a shift from infectious to chronic diseases. This study aims to explore the burden of NCDs in a tertiary care setting, offering insights to inform public health interventions and policies. A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted at Sir Salimullah Medical College Mitford Hospital, Dhaka, involving 6698 patients admitted in 2022 (1st January 2022 to 31st December 2022). Data were collected retrospectively from medical records, focusing on patients above 14 years with NCDs. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS 24.0. Among 6698 admissions, 42.05% were attributed to NCDs. Females exhibited a higher prevalence (56.37%) than males (43.63%). The age group 41-60 years demonstrated the highest NCD prevalence (37.20%). Major NCDs included hypertension (33.22%), diabetes (25.34%), stroke (17.85%) and cardiovascular diseases (12.14%). NCDs contributed to 88.41% of 164 total deaths, with cardiovascular diseases, stroke, chronic respiratory diseases and malignancies as primary causes. In brief, this study sheds light on the critical challenge posed by non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in Bangladesh. With a significant proportion of hospital admissions attributed to NCDs, urgent and targeted interventions are warranted. The observed prominence of NCDs and tha alarming rate of attributed deaths necessitates a shift in healthcare focus. This study's findings emphasize the imperative for innovative approaches, increased resource allocation and heightened awareness campaigns to effectively address the escalating impact of NCDs on both individuals and communities.
