title: WHY EVENTUAL “WINNERS” MAY NOT BE PURSUED: THE CONNECTION BETWEEN INNOVATION PROJECT TYPE AND ABANDONMENT ERROR OCCURRENCE
abstract: Innovation project termination is inherently uncertain, and firms may sometimes abandon projects that would ultimately have succeeded. We conceptualise such outcomes as abandonment errors and develop a process model explaining how they arise. Specifically, we argue that innovation project type shapes perceived project uncertainty, which influences the extent to which decision-makers rely on rationality and intuition, thereby affecting abandonment quality and, ultimately, abandonment error occurrence. Using survey data on abandoned projects from U.S. managers with innovation decision authority, we find that more exploratory (as opposed to exploitative) innovation projects are perceived as more uncertain and are more likely to be evaluated intuitively. Greater reliance on intuition lowers abandonment quality, whereas a more extensive use of rationality leads to a higher decision quality. However, a higher decision quality is ultimately crucial to decreasing the possibility of abandonment error occurrence. These findings advance research on innovation project termination by showing that abandonment errors emerge not only from project characteristics, but also from how uncertainty is processed in the abandonment decision itself. For managers, the results underscore the importance of structuring evaluations of uncertain projects carefully.
venue: International Journal of Innovation Management

title: Supranational Banking Supervision, Credit Supply, and Risk‐Taking: European Evidence from Multi‐Country Credit Registers
abstract: ABSTRACT Using a novel data set of multi‐country credit registers and an institutional change from national to supranational supervision, we show that supranational banking supervision can increase credit supply while mitigating excessive risk‐taking. Supranational supervision increases credit supply only in financially stressed countries while reducing the credit supply to the riskiest (zombie) firms. These improved lending effects stem from weaker national institutions, differential national supervisory incentives, lower national supervisory abilities, and weaker national insolvency laws. Moreover, improved access to external finance from wholesale and bond markets as well as lower risk‐weighted assets allow supranationally supervised banks to expand the supply of credit. Overall, despite some supranational supervisory arbitrage, supranational supervision decreases firm‐level credit to the riskiest firms while increasing firm‐level credit availability in stressed countries without reducing it in nonstressed countries.
venue: The Journal of Finance

title: Evolution of a community-based outdoor tourism and recreation resource into a public-private partnership, a social-ecological systems approach
abstract: This qualitative study employs a Social-Ecological Systems (SES) approach to explore and understand the evolution of a community-based outdoor tourism resource into a public-private partnership, using the Hump Ridge Track, New Zealand, as a case study. While community-based tourism initiatives face challenges such as profitability and governance, characteristics that enable successful development into a public-private partnership have not yet been identified. This study addresses this gap by examining factors and stakeholder dynamics that are crucial to this development. Data were collected using semi-structured expert interviews with purposely selected respondents and document analysis of relevant reports, media releases, and newspaper articles. Governance, visitor types, the transition process, nature-protection, ongoing issues, and community benefits emerged as themes. The SES framework proved useful in explaining how characteristics of actors, governance arrangements, and system conditions interact to generate observed outcomes, demonstrating how SES can be an effective research instrument in complex tourism governance settings.
venue: Tourism Management Perspectives

title: Meaning-Fields, Living Zero-Points, and Non-Stationary External Centers A Dynamical Account of Meaning-Systems and Its Implications for Artificial General Intelligence
abstract: Abstract: We model meaning-systems — religions, ideologies and value-systems — as dynamical objects, and ask what an uncontrollable, non-stationary external center, of which a mature artificial general intelligence (AGI) is the salient candidate, does to human meaning-autonomy. The footing is the Principle of Nonuniformity: an open system is continuously driven off its passive baseline, the law it relaxes to when the drive is withdrawn; the structure it grows is measured by a signed structural stock and governed by a budget master equation whose three expenditures all multiply the stock. Defining meaning as a global orienting gradient, we show that a meaning-field without sustained work relaxes to a dead zero-point — its passive baseline, which for a coupled field is a concentrated default rather than a uniform state — and that meaning-systems are the sustained source holding it at a living zero-point: ritual re-enactment supplies the minimum maintenance, and intergenerational transmission keeps the cultural ratchet from slipping. The morphology of world religions is unified as one sacred/profane stochastic sequence differentiated along two degrees of freedom, coordinate and reading, which give three coordinates by two readings; mystical union occupies the non-aggregated zero of the original coordinate, and a tradition is placed by how its increments depend on accumulated sacredness, not by the shape of a distribution. Modern quiescence is of the satiety type, read as the crossing of an interior optimum of pressure. We then argue that competitive pressure makes outsourcing governance to a superhuman-efficiency center nearly irresistible, and that such a center amplifies the direction each distribution already has: it concentrates a population onto few meaning-systems while flattening or polarising the meaning-weight within persons, and, by controlling the informational substrate of transmission, starves non-conforming systems of their maintenance. Two questions are kept apart. On the detection side the replacement is hard to recognise, because its drift never changes sign and at the limit it rewrites the observable itself. On the side of wall type it is a strong absorbing barrier only if every channel of meaning-regeneration not mediated by the center has gone; the passage there can be a fold, because co-present channels are conjunctive; whether a residue survives every finite efficiency pressure is decided by the tail of the cost of removing those channels; and the wall type is measured by recovery decay rates and a release test, never by a variance. Both statements about AGI are tier C and hold only for a passive object. Five predictions are registered, and the point at which the value choice of a precautionary pause enters is stated.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Green Fashion Revolution: From Waste to Innovation
abstract: Abstract The fashion industry is experiencing a major environmental challenge while continuing to play an important role in creativity, culture, employment and economic activity. The rapid growth of fast fashion has made clothing more affordable and accessible, but it has also encouraged high production volumes, short product lifetimes and increasing textile waste. This paper examines green innovation as a pathway for moving fashion away from a linear “take–make–dispose” model towards a more sustainable and circular system. The study uses a qualitative review of secondary literature and reports from recognised environmental organisations, with particular attention to sustainable materials, circular design, textile recycling, cleaner processing, digital technologies, business-model innovation and consumer behaviour. The review indicates that no single material or technology can make fashion sustainable. Instead, meaningful change requires coordinated innovation throughout the product lifecycle. Designers can contribute by developing durable, repairable, adaptable and recyclable garments; manufacturers can reduce water, energy and chemical impacts; businesses can introduce resale, rental, repair and take-back systems; and consumers can extend garment life through responsible use and care. The paper argues that green fashion should be understood as a system-level transformation rather than simply a marketing category. It concludes that the strongest pathway for the future is the integration of environmental responsibility with creativity, technology, cultural knowledge and viable business practices.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Digital Financial Inclusion and Urban Economic Resilience in China: Evidence from a Double Machine Learning Approach
abstract: Strengthening urban economic resilience is critical for sustaining stable economic growth amid frequent external shocks and ongoing structural economic transformation in China. As a core financial paradigm in the digital era, digital financial inclusion (DFI) requires systematic examination of its long-term macroeconomic stabilization effects. This study investigates the effect of DFI on urban economic resilience, explores its underlying transmission mechanisms, and determines heterogeneous effects across regional and urban characteristics. Based on panel data of 334 prefecture-level-and-above cities in China from 2011 to 2023, this study constructs a multi-dimensional urban economic resilience capacity index that reflects cities’ latent systemic capacity to resist, recover, adapt, and transform in response to exogenous shocks. Employing a double machine learning (DML) framework to address potential nonlinearities and complex functional relationships, this study provides robust empirical evidence of a positive relationship between DFI and urban economic resilience. The exploration of transmission mechanisms indicates that technological innovation, industrial structure upgrading, and consumption upgrading serve as potential paths. Heterogeneity analyses further indicate that the resilience-boosting effects of DFI vary across geographic regions, DFI dimensions, urban attributes and policy contexts, being notably larger in eastern, non-resource-based, core, and “Broadband China” pilot cities. These findings yield targeted policy implications, emphasizing the need for regionally differentiated DFI strategies and a balanced development paradigm between empowerment efficiency and risk governance. This study offers critical empirical insights and a reliable reference for leveraging DFI to foster high-quality, shock-resistant, and sustainable urban economic development.
venue: Sustainability

title: Attachment Styles and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Among Trauma-Exposed Older Adults: Evidence From a non-Western Context
abstract: This study aimed to examine the relationship between post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and attachment styles among older adults exposed to traumatic events. A descriptive–correlational design was employed using a stratified random sample of 534 participants from Irbid Governorate, Jordan. The study makes three key contributions to the literature by addressing the underrepresentation of elderly populations in trauma research, particularly within non-Western and Arab contexts. Data were collected using validated measures of PTSD and attachment styles. The findings indicated that PTSD symptoms and attachment styles were present at moderate levels. Anxious attachment was the most prevalent style, followed by avoidant and secure attachment. Correlation analysis revealed that secure attachment was negatively associated with PTSD, whereas anxious and avoidant attachment styles showed significant positive associations with PTSD symptoms. These findings highlight the dual role of attachment styles as both protective and risk factors in trauma-related outcomes. The results underscore the importance of developing culturally sensitive interventions that enhance secure attachment, strengthen social support, and improve emotional regulation among older adults. The study provides valuable cross-cultural evidence that contributes to the global understanding of PTSD and attachment processes in later life
venue: North American journal of psychology

title: Charting the life of Billboard hits through memory, turnover and predictability
abstract: Abstract Rankings shape the visibility and success of cultural products, yet their temporal dynamics remain underexplored when comparing distinct ranked objects within the same domain. Here, we use nearly seven decades of Billboard Hot 100 songs and six decades of Billboard 200 albums to investigate how success emerges, persists and differs between songs and albums. We find that albums exhibit a heavier-tailed permanence distribution and re-enter the charts more often than songs, whereas songs typically have longer uninterrupted runs. Similarity between successive charts decays much faster for songs than for albums, suggesting that individual hits reflect shorter-lived collective attention, while albums retain longer cultural memory. Rank-turbulence divergence (RTD) shows that consecutive charts are similar, but that top positions are dominated more by rank reshuffling than by turnover. Entropy-based analyses reveal high uncertainty in rank movements, with distinct historical patterns for songs and albums and a strong dependence on trajectory length. Clustering of trajectories shows that chart success is organized into a small number of typical pathways, including canonical rise-and-fall trajectories, high-end persistence and monotonic decline. Together, these results show that musical charts are not merely records of popularity, but dynamic memory systems in which attention, turnover and predictability interact differently for songs and albums.
venue: Royal Society Open Science

title: "Sustainable Accounting Practices and Financial Resilience of MSMEs: An Empirical Study of MSMEs in Kolhapur District, Maharashtra"
abstract: Abstract: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises, also called MSMEs, play a vital role in creating jobs, boosting local economies, encouraging entrepreneurship and generating income. Yet MSMEs face hurdles. The environment is full of pressure from nature, changing expectations from stakeholders, new rules, limited resources and financial uncertainty. In such a setting, sustainable accounting practices give MSMEs information about environmental costs, how much resources they consume, the money spent on sustainability and their performance in environmental, social and governance areas, known as ESG. This data helps MSMEs make decisions, control costs, use resources more efficiently and manage risks. All of this strengthens resilience. This study investigates the link between accounting practices and financial resilience in MSMEs located in Kolhapur District, Maharashtra. The study blends ideas from Stakeholder Theory, the Resource‐Based View and the Natural Resource‐Based View to show how sustainable accounting practices build capabilities inside MSMEs and boost resilience. Sustainable accounting information, green and environmental accounting and ESG and sustainability reporting are seen as the parts of sustainable accounting practices. Financial resilience is measured by how MSMEs can handle rising costs, changes in revenue, sudden financial pressure, risk and resource needs. This study uses a descriptive and analytical research design. We will gather data from about 100 MSME owners, entrepreneurs, managers, accountants and finance staff using a structured five‐point Likert‐scale questionnaire. We will analyse the data with statistics Cronbach’s alpha, Pearson correlation and multiple regression to test the proposed links. This study aims to add to the growing literature on accounting by moving focus from usual financial performance measures to financial resilience and by giving regional evidence from MSMEs in Kolhapur District.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: How much habituation is enough? An R application for ad hoc content-related limits of acceptance in behavioral research
abstract: Abstract Evaluating test–retest reliability is of crucial importance for clinical decision-making and an integral component of studies in empirical sciences. In psychology, classical test theory focused on reliability coefficients, but research has shown that intraclass correlation coefficients and Cronbach’s alpha have limited value in quantifying individual measurement error sources appropriately. Preliminary assumptions such as parallel readings and independency of error sources are violated by practice/habituation effects, i.e., test–retest systematic errors. Although awareness of the need for additional measurement quantifications to properly assess test–retest agreement has increased, many such quantifications are insufficiently implemented. Furthermore, one of the most important agreement analyses introduced by Bland and Altman in 1986 has interpretation limitations, as the limits of agreement are descriptive and not linked to content-based clinical decision-making, oftentimes causing inappropriate usage. To counteract these limitations and improve the implementation of agreement analyses in addition to more commonly used reliability coefficients, we introduce a software package that allows predefining acceptable measurement limits (limits of acceptance) to evaluate the sufficiency of task habituation to gauge individual error sources. The package implements a comprehensive test–retest evaluation in order to improve transparency of data quality reporting in psychological and cognitive research.
venue: Behavior Research Methods

title: Digital-Real-Economy Integration for Sustainable Industrial Chain Resilience: Patent Citation Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
abstract: Industrial chain resilience (ICR) is increasingly important for sustainable industrial development, yet firm-level evidence on how digital-real-economy integration (DRI) affects ICR remains limited. This study aims to examine the impact of DRI on ICR and its underlying mechanisms. We hypothesize that DRI enhances ICR directly and through technological innovation, human-capital upgrading, and improved total factor productivity (TFP). Using 16,188 firm-year observations of Chinese listed firms from 2013 to 2024, we construct a patent citation-based measure of DRI and a multidimensional ICR index. Fixed-effects regressions, instrumental variable tests, robustness checks, and mediation analyses show that DRI significantly improves ICR. The effect operates through broader technological knowledge, higher innovation efficiency and R&D investment, upgraded human capital, and increased TFP. Heterogeneity analyses further show stronger effects among firms with weaker financing constraints, regions with stronger intellectual property protection and more advanced digital infrastructure. These findings provide micro-level evidence that digital–real technological integration contributes to resilient and sustainable industrial development.
venue: Sustainability

title: Support Needs and Stigma in Online Mental Health Discussions: Evidence from Large-Scale Comment Analysis
abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to characterize mental health discourse in user comments on YouTube videos about depression and bipolar disorder, focusing on how personal experience, stigma, and community building are expressed in digital interactions.Methods: A total of 100 videos were identified using the keywords “depression” and “bipolar disorder.” Using the YouTube API, video metadata and 16,241 comments were collected. Most videos were produced by individual doctors, media outlets, and general hospitals, focusing on treatment, diagnosis, and symptoms. After removing non-informative, duplicated, or commercial posts, 13,183 comments were analyzed. Using GPT-5, comments were classified into eight predefined categories.Results: “Personal Experience” was the most frequent category (9,551), followed by “Needs for Community Building: Emotional” (3,842) and “Needs for Community Building: Instrumental” (2,873). Actual “Community Building: Emotional Support” (1,345) and “Community Building: Instrumental Support” (549) appeared less frequently. Stigma-related discourse included “Social Stigma” (1,717) and “Internalized Stigma” (1,184), while “Non-evidence-based Advice” appeared in 1,146 comments. Co-occurrence analysis revealed strong associations between “Personal Experience” and “Needs for Community Building: Emotional” (.56), “Needs for Community Building: Instrumental” (.36), and “Internalized Stigma” (.33).Conclusion: Expert mental health video comment sections functioned primarily as experience- and emotion-centered spaces where users expressed substantial emotional and informational needs but received limited reciprocal support. These findings highlight the need for digital mental health environments integrating evidence-based information with structured support frameworks.
venue: Research in Community and Public Health Nursing

title: Contested Liberalisms in Mexico: Popular Liberalism, the Fourth Transformation, and the Struggle over Constitutional Identity
abstract: Mexico's Cuarta Transformación (4T) is usually read as one instance of a global illiberal turn. This article argues instead that the Mexican constitutional conflict is internal to the liberal-republican tradition: rival projects each claim the mantle of liberalism to define who counts as 'the people'. Drawing on scholarship on popular and plebeian liberalism in Spanish America, it shows that the 4T advances by appropriating a popular, Juarista liberalism against a proprietary one it codes as neoporfirista. Four frameworks — comparative law, legitimation theory, alterity and imagined communities — are applied to presidential discourse, three constitutional reforms and political cartoons, and synthesised through a Constitutional Legitimacy Vector (CLV). The appropriation reconfigures who counts as 'the people' and why citizens obey, producing a structural decoupling resistant to procedural resolution. The case refines the theory of illiberalism: Latin American populism can operate through appropriation of the liberal lineage, not its negation.
venue: INGURUAK REVISTA VASCA DE SOCIOLOGÍA Y CIENCIA POLÍTICA
categories: Politics and Society in Latin America

title: Diagnosing ANOVA‐Based Gauge R&R Models: Why Raw Measurements and Model Residuals Provide Different Information
abstract: ABSTRACT Gauge Repeatability and Reproducibility (Gauge R&R) studies are widely used to quantify measurement system variability. When variance components are estimated using Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), the validity of the results depends on assumptions concerning the fitted model and its error term. However, many practical implementations rely on the raw measurements, which contain the combined effects of parts, operators, interactions, and measurement error. Consequently, diagnostics performed on raw measurements do not necessarily provide direct evidence regarding ANOVA assumptions. This study investigates how diagnostic conclusions depend on whether analyses are performed on raw measurements or on ANOVA residuals. Monte Carlo simulations evaluate seven normality tests under different experimental designs, variance‐component scenarios, and residual distributions. Two illustrative datasets complement the simulations and demonstrate situations in which raw‐data and residual‐based diagnostics lead to different conclusions. Graphical methods, including Q–Q plots, boxplots, control charts, and an exploratory GLRAM‐based biplot, are also examined. The results show that normality tests applied to raw measurements characterize the marginal distribution of observed responses, which includes part, operator, interaction, and measurement‐error effects, whereas residual‐based diagnostics directly assess model assumptions. The study supports a two‐stage diagnostic strategy: raw measurements should be explored to understand measurement‐system behavior, while model residuals should be analyzed to assess the adequacy of the fitted ANOVA model.
venue: Quality and Reliability Engineering International

title: The embodied real effective exchange rate: measuring cost competitiveness in global value chains
abstract: Abstract We propose the embodied real effective exchange rate (EREER), a measure of cost competitiveness at the country-sector level, accounting for global value chains. We derive it from a single Armington-CES framework with intermediate-input linkages. It departs in three respects from conventional REERs, which are predominantly constructed at the national level. First, it is constructed for individual country-sectors, each compared with the same sector abroad; indices for sectoral groups and entire economies follow by aggregation. Second, its deflator is the sector’s embodied unit labor costs, which incorporate labor-cost developments along the entire production chain at home and abroad, rather than in the sector alone. Third, its bilateral weights retain the double-weighting scheme of official REER statistics but are computed from the domestic value added in sectoral sales flows rather than from gross flows. Using global input–output data, we compare the EREER with conventional benchmarks at the sector level for German industries and at the country level for 36 economies. At the sector level, discrepancies are often large, and in some industries the measures even disagree on the direction of change; at the country level, they generally agree on the direction but differ in the magnitude and persistence of cumulative changes. In export regressions for country and sector panels, the estimated responsiveness to effective exchange rates is strongest under the EREER across export outcomes.
venue: Review of World Economics

title: The Reconstruction of Coherent Identity in Baby Halder's A Life Less Ordinary
abstract: Title: The Reconstruction of Coherent Identity in Baby Halder’s A Life Less Ordinary First Author: Pariliu GangmeiCo authro: R.K. Ashalata Devi AbstractBaby Halder’s autobiography, A Life Less Ordinary (2013), documents the life of an ordinary domestic worker who stood unabated amid her life crisis. In the book, Baby recollects her lived experiences as an abandoned child, a married woman trapped in a violent marriage, a domestic worker, and subsequently her transformative journey to becoming a writer. She was a victim of child abuse, domestic violence as well as psychological harassment. However, her unyielding resilience and determination have left an indelible mark transforming her struggle into a remarkable strength and a unique representative voice for the marginalized. Baby Halder’s autobiography has primarily been studied through themes of caste, class, gender, patriarchy, marginalization, domestic labor and poverty. But attention to the theoretical functions of Autobiographical Memory remains relatively limited. Hence, the present paper addresses this gap through a close reading of Baby Halder’s autobiography by employing the directive, self, and social functions of autobiographical memory. The present paper examines how memory helps Baby Halder reconstruct her identity, understand her past, respond to the present situation, guide future choices, and maintain social relationships. The paper contends that Baby’s recollection is a transformative process through which her memories from various life events are reconstructed into a coherent sense of self. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates how autobiographical memory enables Baby Halder in transforming her marginalized position into an empowered identity.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Can't Stop: How Context and Individual Traits Influence Effectiveness of Different Gradual Interventions for Infinite Scrolling on Short-Form Video Platforms
abstract: Infinite scrolling on short-form video platforms like TikTok encourages prolonged engagement and post-usage regret. Interventions aim to mitigate such behavior, but their effectiveness may depend on the interplay between intervention type, contextual factors, and individual traits. In a 7-day within-subject randomized field study (N=104), we compared a baseline pop-up and two gradually intensifying design frictions (visual and haptic). We evaluated behavioral changes and user experience using objective and subjective measures. Results showed that the pop-up was initially effective but quickly lost impact, whereas the visual gradual intervention sustained subjective ratings the longest. Bayesian modeling revealed that self-regulation traits moderate how participants responded to the three intervention types. For participants with low impulsivity, the type of intervention had little influence on its subjective effectiveness. For participants with high impulsivity, however, differences between intervention types were substantial, with the explicit baseline pop-up being most effective compared to the novel gradual interventions. Contextual factors, in contrast, showed little influence. These findings suggest that intervention modality and individual differences in self-regulation shape intervention effectiveness.
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive Mobile Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies

title: Growth of Industrial Cooperatives in Maharashtra State: An Analysis Based on the National Cooperative Database
abstract: Abstract Cooperatives have played an important role in the socio-economic and industrial development of Maharashtra. Apart from agricultural credit, sugar and dairy cooperatives, the state has developed a substantial network of agro-processing and industrial cooperative societies. The present study examines the growth and current position of industrial cooperatives in Maharashtra using secondary data obtained primarily from the National Cooperative Database (NCD) of the Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India. The study analyses the historical pattern of registration of agro-processing/industrial cooperatives from the pre-independence period to 2023 and examines their functional status, membership and position at the national level. The NCD data show that Maharashtra had 5,292 agro-processing/industrial cooperative societies in the 2023 database, of which 4,959 were functional, 229 non-functional and 104 under liquidation. These societies had approximately 12.54 lakh members. The historical registration of the data reveals particularly rapid expansion of the agro processing / industrial cooperative societies after 1970, with 2,271 societies registered during 1991–2010 and another 1,862 during 2011–2023. The recent NCD data shows that the number of primary agro-processing/industrial cooperative societies in Maharashtra has reached to 5,587 societies by 15 July 2026. The study concludes that Maharashtra dominates a leading position in India's industrial cooperative sector, although continued emphasis on operational sustainability, modernization, finance, technology and professional management is necessary
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Using large models and time series forecasting for market reaction analysis
abstract: Forecasting financial market movements requires integrating numerical time-series data with semantic information from financial narratives that shape investor behavior. While deep learning has advanced time-series prediction, existing methods often exploit trivial price autocorrelation rather than capturing genuine predictive signals from multimodal sources. We propose the Semantic-Time Fusion Architecture (STFA), which integrates structured market data with GPT-4-supervised FinBERT semantic representations of financial news through three key innovations: delay-aware temporal alignment between text publication and market reaction, semantic-guided attention mechanisms emphasizing news-relevant historical patterns, and multi-scale temporal fusion with multi-objective training to balance accuracy and interpretability. We evaluate our model on a large-scale financial news and stock price dataset using GPT-4 sentiment annotation across stratified high-liquidity stocks with strictly chronological train-validation-test splits (2013–2020 for training, 2021 for validation, 2022–2023 for testing). Sentiment annotations were generated independently for each article without using any future market information, ensuring strict temporal separation and preventing information leakage. Experiments demonstrate that STFA significantly outperforms traditional time-series models, multimodal baselines, and random walk benchmarks on return prediction, where price autocorrelation vanishes, rather than relying on price-level forecasting. Statistical validation with bootstrap confidence intervals, effect size analysis, and Bonferroni-corrected significance tests confirms robust improvements across independent runs. Ablation studies reveal that GPT-4-supervised FinBERT semantic representations provide superior signals compared with lexicon-based sentiment, with each architectural component contributing significantly to performance. This work demonstrates how temporally aligned semantic understanding enhances both predictive accuracy and model interpretability in financial forecasting.
venue: PLoS ONE

title: Delivering on the promise: How corporate culture influences customer benefits in insurance claim handling
abstract: Corporate culture is viewed as an important organizational capability, yet its effects on customer outcomes, particularly under conditions of stress, remain unclear. To address this gap, this study examines claim settlement in the U.S. property–liability insurance industry using insurer-level data and a difference-in-differences design based on disaster exposure. We analyze claim duration, payment likelihood, and inverse loss ratio. The results reveal a striking asymmetry across market segments. Following disaster shocks, insurers exhibiting higher scores in corporate culture resolve claims faster and are more likely to pay in commercial lines, while effects are largely absent in personal lines. This heterogeneity is consistent with institutional differences across commercial and personal insurance that may shape managerial discretion and coordination, although our empirical design does not distinguish this mechanism from other potential explanations. These results show that corporate culture may function as an operational capability whose influence on claim-settlement outcome varies systematically across insurance lines.
venue: Finance research letters

title: Sleep Duration and Health Outcomes by Sex in the KoGES Ansan Cohort: A Cross-Sectional Interaction Analysis
abstract: Objective: To test whether sex modifies the association between habitual sleep duration and health outcomes in middle-aged Korean adults.Methods: We analyzed cross-sectional data from 3,709 participants in the Ansan arm of the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study Phase 2 (2003–2004). Sleep duration was calculated as a weighted 7-day average and categorized as short (<7 hr), reference (7 to <9 hr), or long (≥9 hr). Primary outcomes were body mass index, fasting plasma glucose, a fatigue-related symptom score, and forced expiratory volume in 1 second/forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC) ratio. The primary analysis tested the sleep category×sex interaction using 2-df likelihood-ratio tests adjusted for age, income, marital status, occupation, smoking, drinking, and exercise. Secondary outcomes were controlled using the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate.Results: In the primary fully adjusted model, sleep duration×sex interactions were not significant for body mass index (p=0.930), fasting glucose (p=0.388), fatigue-related symptom score (p=0.104), or FEV1/FVC ratio (p=0.855). A complementary short-versus-reference 1-df interaction contrast was nominally significant for fatigue-related symptom score (p=0.047). In an explicitly post hoc age-stratified analysis, the fatigue-related symptom score interaction was concentrated among participants aged <50 years (p=0.001): short sleep was associated with higher adjusted fatigue-related symptom scores in women (+4.75 points; 95% confidence interval [CI], +2.33 to +7.16) but not in men (-0.50; 95% CI, -2.52 to +1.52).Conclusion: This analysis found no evidence of broad sex modification for cardiometabolic or pulmonary outcomes. The younger-adult fatigue-related symptom score signal should be considered hypothesis-generating pendingreplication with validated fatigue measures and longitudinal data. The fatigue-related symptom score used in this study was not a validated fatigue instrument, which limits the interpretability of the fatigue findings.
venue: Chronobiology in Medicine

title: Kepastian Hukum Gugat Cerai ( Khulu’ ) Dalam Pasal 148 Instruksi Presiden Nomor 1 Tahun 1991 Tentang Kompilasi Hukum Islam
abstract: Abstrak : Khulu’ didalam syariat islam sebagaimana diketahui secara umum sebagai gugat cerai, merupakan perceraian yang terjadi karena permintaan istri yang dengan permintaan cerai tersebut istri dipersyaratkan untuk memberikan tebusan “iwadl” kepada suami, ada pendapat ahli fiqh yang memperbolehkan cerai gugat “Khulu’” tanpa adanya tebusan “iwadl” ada juga ahli fiqh yang mewajibkan adanya “iwadl” sebagai syarat sah nya Khulu’. Tujuan dari penelitian ini untuk mengetahui kepastian hukum mengenai “iwald” sebagai syarat sahnya “Khulu’” sebagaimana yang ditentukan dalam pasal 148 Instruksi Presiden Nomor 1 Tahun 1991 tentang Kompilasi Hukum Islam. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode penilitian yuridis normatif yang didapatkan dari data kepustakaan, yang memunculkan kesimpulan bahwa peraturan yang mengatur terkait proses peradilan yang ada selama ini tidak memberikan kepastian hukum, hal ini terdapat didalam pasal 148 ayat (6) Instruksi Presiden Nomor 1 Tahun 1991 tentang Kompilasi Hukum Islam yang menyatakan bahwa apabila tidak tercapai kesepakatan tentang besarnya “iwadl” Pengadilan Agama memeriksa dan memutus sebagai perkara biasa, hal tersebut bertolak belakang dengan pemahaman mayoritas ahli fiqh yang mana mereka berpendapat bahwa syarat sahnya gugat cerai mewajibkan adanya tebusan “iwadl”, “iwadl” sendiri disimbolkan sebagi hak suami, apabila hak tersebut tidak ditunaikan maka syarat sahnya gugat cerai tidak dapat terpenuhi, Tinjauan dari teori, pendapat para sarjana dan para ahli fiqh diharapkan dapat memberikan titik terang terhadap permasalahan gugat cerai ini, karena sejatinya gugat cerai sendiri merupakan syariat islam yang dikodifikasikan kedalam sebuah Instruksi Presiden Nomor 1 Tahun 1991 tentang Kompilasi Hukum Islam. Kata Kunci : Gugat cerai, Kepastian hukum
venue: Ubaya Repository (University of Surabaya)

title: Artificial Intelligence in Personal Finance Management: An Empirical Study of Young Investors in the Kalyan Region
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is embedded in every financial transaction and interaction through robo-advising, auto- Recommendations, portfolios tracking, digital financial assistants, and financial information processing tools. This paper considers the relevance of AI to young investors of the Kalyan Region. Using relevant published evidence from SEBI, NSE, AMFI and RBI, along with peer-reviewed research and analysis, this paper applies descriptive, comparative and trend-oriented analysis to examine the use and impact of AI in personal finance management. Evidence shows an ageing-down of India's investor base, with young people constituting an increasing proportion of the registered individual investors. The study finds that AI can reduce information and access barriers and enable personalisation, monitoring, and analysis. However, the benefits are limited by financial literacy, trust, perceived risk, transparency and ability to question AI outputs.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: A Provenance-Preserving Scientific Claim Ledger: Versioned Evidence, Supersession, and Auditable Correction Without Historical Rewriting
abstract: Scientific knowledge systems routinely revise claims as new evidence appears. Yet many research workflows represent claims as mutable text fields or database rows whose latest value silently replaces earlier states. This creates an audit problem: correction can erase provenance, supersession can obscure which evidence supported which formulation, and later interpretations can inherit support that was collected for materially different claims. This paper presents a domain-specific architecture for scientific claim records that integrates bitemporal non-erasure semantics (Snodgrass 1999; SQL:2011), PROV-O-aligned provenance tracking (Lebo et al. 2013), nanopublication-inspired evidence typing (Groth et al. 2010), and an event-ID replay rule layered on event sourcing (Fowler 2005). The integration includes design elements not identified together in the cited systems: a typed evidence-inheritance function I() for supersession events, a five-state administrative status vocabulary independent of evidentiary state, machine-generated claim lifecycle management via PROPOSED_CLAIM, and typed SPLIT/MERGE operations with provenance threading.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Temporal Asymmetry in Precious Metals and Commodity Currencies: Conditional Lead-Lag Diagnostics on XAUUSD and AUDUSD
abstract: This whitepaper presents an exploratory investigation of temporal asymmetry and lead-lag relationships between gold (XAUUSD) and the Australian dollar (AUDUSD) across multiple temporal windows and market regimes. The study applies a multi-scale lead-lag diagnostic framework to examine whether movements in XAUUSD systematically precede corresponding movements in AUDUSD under different market conditions. The analysis incorporates timestamp alignment, matched-event construction, regime-based filtering, lead-lag detection across multiple bar windows, and permutation-based statistical testing. The results indicate a consistent XAUUSD-leading pattern across the tested lead-lag windows under the analyzed conditions. However, the findings are presented as exploratory evidence rather than as a confirmed generalizable relationship. Out-of-sample (OOS) validation is also examined. The study explicitly documents methodological limitations, including small test-sample sizes in some regimes and the use of full-sample regime thresholds during OOS validation, which introduces a mild look-ahead bias. Consequently, generalization of the observed patterns to other samples or market conditions is not yet confirmed. This work is intended to document an initial empirical exploration and provide a foundation for subsequent research. Future development may include stricter train-only regime threshold estimation, broader cross-asset testing, and evolutionary optimization for systematic discovery of lead-lag conditions.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
categories: Complex Systems and Time Series Analysis

title: Lived experiences of home care nurses during the COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland: A descriptive phenomenological study
abstract: Objective This study explores the lived experiences of home care nurses in Switzerland during the COVID-19 pandemic. It aims to understand how nurses navigated a period marked by uncertainty, emotional strain, changing professional demands, and close proximity to vulnerable patients. Particular attention was paid to how this context shaped their engagement with end-of-life (EOL) discussions and related practices in daily care. Methods A qualitative design with a descriptive phenomenological approach was used. Twelve home care nurses from the Geneva public home care service participated in semi-structured interviews conducted between November 2021 and February 2022. Interviews were analysed following Giorgi's method, and methodological rigour was ensured through triangulation and team discussion. Results The analysis identified six interrelated themes. The first axis described the emotional and professional experiences of nurses during the pandemic. Nurses faced continuous uncertainty and emotional strain but demonstrated adaptive capacities through individual and collective coping strategies. Institutional responses provided both stability and new constraints, while care practices were restructured and professional identities redefined between empowerment and exhaustion. The second axis described engagement with advance care planning (ACP)-related practices in the pandemic context. When conditions allowed, the training fostered confidence and humanity in communication with patients, though its implementation remained limited by organisational, relational, and emotional barriers. In some cases, the reflection initiated professionally extended to the personal sphere. Conclusions The study highlights the complexity and evolving nature of home care nursing during the pandemic. Beyond documenting adaptation under pressure, it underscores the need for sustained institutional support, recognition of nurses' expertise, and clear frameworks for their role in EOL discussions.
venue: Heliyon

title: Morocco's grand strategy: Pillars and limitations
abstract: The Grand Strategy aims to align a state’s means and resources with its strategic priorities in pursuit of national interests, while taking into account internal and external constraints. For Morocco, the Grand Strategy provides a key framework for achieving national interests and redefining the country’s position within the international community. The New Development Model constitutes the backbone of this Grand Strategy and serves as the roadmap to be followed, although it is not the only component. The monarchy remains the primary driving force and impetus behind the Grand Strategy. This article analyzes the components of Morocco’s Grand Strategy, which can be classified into three essential pillars: territorial integrity and internal cohesion, regional positioning and international influence, and inclusive and sustainable economic development. However, the ambitions of this Grand Strategy remain constrained by limitations in internal capacities and resources, as well as by external constraints arising from a challenging international environment. Economic, environmental, and climatic vulnerabilities further exacerbate these constraints.
venue: African Research Reports

title: Multi scale LSTM model construction and NSGA-II optimization method for dynamic threshold of high frequency trading signal
abstract: Forecasting high-frequency trading signals is complicated by microstructure noise, heterogeneous temporal patterns, changing market states, and strict low-latency requirements. This paper constructs a multi-scale LSTM and dynamic threshold attention framework, and adopts a candidate-level multi-objective configuration screening method under deployment constraints. Level 3 order data are transformed into microstructure features that describe large-order flow, order-flow imbalance, order-book pressure, liquidity pressure, high-frequency volatility, and cross-market cointegration residuals. DB4 wavelet decomposition separates high-, medium-, and low-frequency components, which are encoded by independent LSTM branches. Attention sensitivity is conditioned on volatility and liquidity, while NSGA-II searches the configuration space using predictive performance, maximum drawdown, and inference latency as joint objectives. The empirical analysis uses 30 highly active CSI 300 constituents over 240 trading days in 2022. The base multi-scale dynamic-threshold architecture reports an AUC of 0.861, a Sharpe ratio of 5.6, a maximum drawdown of 11.5, and an inference latency of 15.9 μs. The final NSGA-II-selected configuration improves these point estimates to an AUC of 0.867, a Sharpe ratio of 5.8, a maximum drawdown of 10.7, and an inference latency of 12.8 μs. The one-minute forecasting horizon and the 3 to 5 percent volatility regime provide the strongest reported performance for the base architecture. Rolling-window, sector, feature, and event analyses are used to assess robustness without treating descriptive associations as causal evidence.
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences

title: Validation of the Korean Version of the Body Perception Questionnaire–Short Form
abstract: Background: This study examined the factor structure, reliability, and validity of the Korean version of the Body Perception Questionnaire–Short Form (K-BPQ-SF) in Korean adults.Methods: Online survey data from 700 Korean adults were randomly divided into Sample A (n=300) for exploratory factor analysis and Sample B (n=400) for confirmatory factor analysis. Convergent validity was examined using correlations with related external measures in the full sample (N=700).Results: Exploratory factor analysis identified a 23-item, three-factor structure for Body Awareness and a 19-item, two-factor structure for Autonomic Reactivity. In the comparison using the same final 42 items, the modified Korean five-factor model showed a relatively better fit than the original study-based three-factor model. The five subscales demonstrated adequate internal consistency. All five subscales were significantly positively correlated with alexithymia, difficulties in emotion regulation, posttraumatic stress symptoms, and trait anxiety, whereas they were significantly negatively correlated with social connectedness. These findings are consistent with a priori theoretical predictions and support the convergent validity of the K-BPQ-SF.Conclusions: These findings support the reliability and validity of the K-BPQ-SF as a self-report measure of body awareness and autonomic reactivity in Korean adults. Implications for its application and directions for future research are discussed.
venue: Korean Journal of Stress Research

title: ON THE SOUL OF ANIMALS AND THEIR RIGHTS - RIGOROUS SUPPORT IN THE ACTION HUMANKIND OWES
abstract: The understanding that a person is required or expected to have of themselves must inevitably be linked to their presence in the world as an individual. This sense of self has traditionally remained distant for anthropos, but this existing distance does not eliminate the biological reality or the moral responsibility faced by everyone in the human world. All this is reinforced by the fact that the emergence of humankind, and probably its extinction too, are merely stages in the development of nature, independent of its subjective will or interests. This is why what comes to the fore are not so much the differences between members of the fauna, which are obvious and easily discernible, as the similarities, whose apparent clarity often leads to their underestimation and conceptual neglect. This article examines an ecosophical problem concerning animal rights - viewed not so much as a legal fiction, but as an ethical duty that binds the human animal to responsibility within its creative actions and the rational morality from which they stem.
venue: E-Journal VFU

title: Population-Level Data Linkages in Worldwide Twin Research Resources
abstract: Twin registries are foundational resources for research in behavioral and medical genetics, epidemiology, and public health. Over several decades, successive international reviews have documented their expansion in number, geographical coverage, phenotypic scope, molecular profiling, and participation in large-scale collaborations. This overview first traces this development through previous global overviews of twin registries and then examines record linkage as an increasingly important feature of contemporary twin research. Drawing on diverse twin registries, twin cohorts, multi-cohort resources, and international consortia, we describe how twin data are linked to population and administrative registers, health and educational records, biobanks, and environmental and geospatial data. Microdata linkage connects individual-level twin phenotypes with longitudinal administrative, clinical, educational, and molecular information, extending follow-up and supporting life-course analyses. Macrodata linkage incorporates contextual information on neighborhood environments, socioeconomic conditions, and policy settings, enabling individual and familial differences to be studied within broader social and environmental contexts. Comparison across resources demonstrates substantial variation in the scope and implementation of record linkage, from established national linkage systems to partial, domain-specific, and planned linkages, shaped by differences in legal frameworks, consent models, data governance, and secure access infrastructures. By placing current record linkage practices within the historical development of twin research resources, this overview shows how linkage extends the classical twin design through longitudinal, multi-domain, and contextual data, broadening its potential for research on health, behavior, and development across the life course.
venue: Twin Research and Human Genetics

title: Spatial Econometrics of Urban Well-being: Resolving the Growth-Equity Paradox Across the 50 Largest U.S. Metropolitan Statistical Areas
abstract: Conventional urban performance metrics predominantly rely on macroeconomic aggregates, obscuring localized socio-spatial divergence and the spatial dependencies governing municipal ecosystems. This study establishes a replicable spatial-econometric framework to evaluate urban Quality of Life (QOL) equity across the 50 largest Metropolitan Statistical Areas (MSAs) in the United States. Leveraging 2021 U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates integrated with built-environment and ecological datasets, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was deployed to construct an orthogonal composite index (Ultimate QOLI) without subjective weighting biases. Factor loadings revealed that the Gini Index (+0.6366) and Housing Affordability (+0.5899) act as primary structural drivers of spatial polarization, while Median Household Income loaded negatively (-0.4225), demonstrating that unbridled economic expansion detached from redistributive mechanisms systematically accelerates socio-spatial exclusion.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Digital Ageism and Ageism Among Middle-Aged and Older Adults and the Mediating Role of Expectations Regarding Aging: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Purpose: This study examined whether expectations regarding aging mediate the relationship between ageism and digital ageism among middle-aged and older adults and whether this indirect effect differs by age group.Methods: A cross-sectional design was employed to analyze the data of 300 South Korean adults aged 45 years or older, recruited via an online research panel through sampling stratified by age and gender. Ageism, expectations regarding aging, and digital ageism were assessed using validated self-report scales. Mediation and moderated mediation were tested using Hayes’ PROCESS Models 4 and 14 with bias-corrected bootstrapping.Results: Digital ageism was positively correlated with ageism (r=.41, p<.001) and negatively correlated with expectations regarding aging (r=-.37, p<.001). Expectations regarding aging partially mediated the relationship between ageism and digital ageism (B=0.22; 95% boot CI=0.11-0.35). Middle-aged adults showed higher digital ageism than older adults (t=2.90, p=.004); however, the mediating pathway did not differ by age group.Conclusions: The findings suggest that expectations regarding aging may play a mediating role in the association between ageism and digital ageism. Interventions to reduce digital ageism should target both ageist beliefs and negative expectations regarding aging and should be implemented starting in midlife rather than focusing exclusively on older adulthood.
venue: Research in Community and Public Health Nursing

title: “It’s not that I don’t have a life, it’s that I choose to have many”: A Qualitative Exploration of Video Gamers’ Perceived Motivations for Gaming and their Impact on Psychological Health.
abstract: While several factors have been highlighted as either facilitators or inhibitors of basic psychological needs in video gaming, there is little evidence to identify the specific mechanisms by which these effects operate. Using qualitative semi-structured online interviews with 15 video game players (MAge = 38.28, SD = 12.65) and analysed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis, this study explored experiences in video games and gaming culture that provided either a source of need satisfaction or need frustration. Participants discussed experiences that provided a sense of competence, mood management, social connection, and positive disengagement, as well as experiences that could be unfair, unpleasant, toxic, or generally stress-inducing. This study highlights specific factors that promote positive well-being and contribute to negative well-being in players and illustrates less-explored experiential factors that are vital to video gaming as a psychologically restorative activity.

title: Changing Patterns of Capital Structure in Indian Companies: An Empirical Longitudinal Analysis of NIFTY 50 (2016–17 to 2025–26)
abstract: Abstract Capital structure represents a vital component of corporate financial decision-making because it determines the relative use of debt and equity in financing business activities. Changes in macroeconomic conditions, interest rate cycles, industry-specific risks, profitability, and corporate expansion strategies heavily influence financing choices. This study examines the changing patterns of capital structure among leading Indian listed companies using the NIFTY 50 index constituents as a fixed sample over a ten-year period from 2016–17 to 2025–26 (500 firm-year observations). Secondary financial data were extracted from consolidated financial statements on Screener.in and annual disclosures. Key indicators—including the Debt–Equity Ratio (DER), Debt-to-Assets Ratio (DAR), Equity-to-Assets Ratio (EAR), Profitability, Firm Size, and Asset Tangibility—were rigorously analyzed using descriptive statistics, Compound Annual Growth Rates (CAGR), one-way ANOVA, Pearson correlation, and panel regression models. The empirical findings reveal that over the study period, the grand average Debt–Equity Ratio stood at 0.84 (median: 0.46), while the average Debt-to-Assets Ratio was 24.03%. Aggregate total corporate borrowings grew at a CAGR of 8.68%, whereas total equity expanded at a CAGR of 10.04%. ANOVA testing indicates no statistically significant change in average leverage over time across the 10 years (p = 1.000), but confirms highly statistically significant structural variation across industry sectors (F = 100.22, p < 0.0001). Non-bank financial services and aviation exhibit the highest leverage, whereas FMCG, IT, and defense capital goods maintain near-zero debt policy. Regression analysis confirms that firm profitability is inversely related to leverage, validating the Pecking Order Theory in the Indian corporate landscape.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Quality Infrastructure and Sustainable Bilateral China–Africa Trade: Evidence from National Standards
abstract: Can national standards, as a core component of national quality infrastructure (NQI), facilitate the sustainable development of South–South trade, or do they instead create barriers to market access? We examine this question by combining China’s industry-level national standards with highly disaggregated bilateral trade data for 52 African countries over 2002–2019. Using PPML models with country-product and country-year fixed effects, we find that Chinese national standards are associated with significantly higher imports from African countries, while no significant effect is found for China’s exports to Africa. Mechanism analysis shows that standards are associated with greater firm participation in African sourcing and higher imported-product quality. National standards are significantly positively correlated with the expansion of imported product varieties. Significant positive associations are found for resource-manufactured products and technology-manufactured products. It is also more pronounced for African countries with greater quality infrastructure capacity and for recommended, technical, and internationally aligned national standards. Aid for trade further strengthens the trade effects of standardization. These findings show that national standards can support the economic and structural sustainability of China–Africa trade by broadening market participation, improving product quality, and promoting trade diversification and structural upgrading, with these effects depending on partner-country quality infrastructure capacity and complementary trade-supporting institutions.
venue: Sustainability

title: Scaleval — Appreciation and Potential Measurement Protocol (v2)
abstract: This version builds on the founding document (v1) by formalising the protocol’s operational mechanisms: the appreciation unit (the bill), the calculated metrics (Potential, Cumulative Potential, Conviction Rate), the economic grammar of the system, the inter-Potence conversion mechanism (SES), status titles, and the Scaleval Time module — a core component of the protocol. It also provides, in response to several critical analyses, a rigorous formulation of what the protocol actually measures — calibrated appreciations, never potential itself in any objective sense — through a five-step cycle running from appreciation to the observed future outcome. This version remains a working paper; several mechanisms remain core.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Enterprise AI Is a Platform Problem: GKS-5, A Reference Architecture for Governed Knowledge Systems
abstract: GKS-5: A Reference Architecture for Governed Knowledge Systems presents an enterprise architecture for governing AI-enabled knowledge systems as they move from isolated experimentation toward operational use. The paper argues that enterprise AI should be treated as a platform and governance problem rather than only as a model-selection problem. It introduces a structured reference architecture for controlling how enterprise knowledge is accessed, transformed, evaluated, governed, and consumed by AI-enabled applications and agents. GKS-5 focuses on the architectural separation of knowledge, governance, policy, assurance, identity, provenance, and execution concerns. The objective is to provide organizations with a practical foundation for building AI systems that remain auditable, policy-aware, explainable, and manageable across heterogeneous enterprise environments. The work is intended for enterprise architects, AI platform teams, security and governance practitioners, researchers, and organizations designing trusted AI and agentic systems.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Identifying a hidden market within the supported housing system in England: The value of a commercial determinants of health lens
abstract: This article broadens understanding of the Commercial Determinants of Health (CDoH) by applying this lens to supported housing, specifically non-commissioned supported exempt accommodation in England. While this housing type is required to operate not-for-profit as part of the welfare system, we illustrate how a ‘hidden market’ has emerged, creating for-profit opportunities for private gain, with harmful consequences for public health. The article draws on documentary analysis of government and academic reports to make a novel contribution to the CDoH field. We identify three ‘profit lanes’ for commercial gain with ramifications for public health: 1) a leasing model that allows property owners to extract profit from Housing Benefit payments, creating opportunity costs for public spending on public health; 2) strategic selection of lucrative places to invest capital for profit rather than in response to welfare needs, which risks undermining housing quality and tenant wellbeing; and 3) overcharging for support and housing services beyond covering costs, which risks undermining tenants’ income security, voice and control as key determinants of health. A CDoH lens and the concepts of a hidden market and profit lanes could be applied to analyse other areas of the welfare system in England that provide social goods (e.g., education) and in other country contexts.
venue: Critical Social Policy

title: Effects of Interpersonal Traumatic Experiences and Interpersonal Problems on Psychological Symptoms among College Students: Moderated Mediating Effect of Expressive Flexibility
abstract: Background: This study examined whether interpersonal problems mediated the relationship between subjective distress from interpersonal trauma and psychological symptoms, and whether emotional expression flexibility moderated this indirect effect.Methods: Self-reported measures were completed by 241 college students with interpersonal trauma experiences. Data were analyzed using correlation, mediation, and moderated mediation analyses. PROCESS Macro for SPSS was used.Results: Interpersonal problems partially mediated the relationship between interpersonal trauma-related distress and psychological symptoms. Furthermore, emotional expression enhancement significantly moderated the association between interpersonal trauma-related distress and problems; conversely, emotional expression suppression did not. The indirect effect through interpersonal problems was significant only at low and average levels of emotional expression enhancement.Conclusions: Emotional expression enhancement may buffer the negative effects of interpersonal trauma on interpersonal problems and psychological symptoms. These findings suggest that interventions for enhancing context-appropriate emotional expression may be useful for college students with interpersonal trauma experiences.
venue: Korean Journal of Stress Research

title: The Voynich Manuscript "Apparatus" Drawings and the Distillation-Apparatus Tradition: A Divergence-Dominant Comparison
abstract: Within the inspected Voynich substrate and named comparator set, the imagery is containment- and immersion-dominant and the record contains no supported identification of a depicted still, alembic, retort, athanor, condensing arm, receiver flask, or furnace. This is an inventory-bounded divergence finding, not a universal proof that no apparatus-like form occurs anywhere in the manuscript. The decisive Quire-13 tube-topology comparison and direct image inspection of several external apparatus witnesses remain open. No direct-transmission or source-identity claim is made.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
